articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.summary: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina
articles.keyPoints:
• India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina
• Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.
• The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.summary: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society
articles.keyPoints:
• This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society
• A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.
• One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.summary: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
articles.keyPoints:
• Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
• If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.
• In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: V-Xpress building key logistics hubs in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under Southern expansion, the company will cover cities like Mangalore, Davangere, Gulbarga, Bijapur, Sirsi, Bagalkot, and Devanahalli, alongside industrial zones in Harohalli, Jigani, Bidadi, and Hindupur

V-Xpress, the Mumbai-headquartered express cargo arm of V-Trans (India) Ltd, is sharpening its focus on South India, targeting key hubs, including Bengaluru and the industrial clusters of Narasapura and Dabaspet, as it expands its services in the region.

The logistics firm said it would open more than 15 new outlets across Karnataka, a move expected to generate over 150 local jobs and focus on Appointment Delivery service for the quick commerce and organised retail sectors. An appointment delivery is a pre-arranged date and time slot agreed upon by the shipper, carrier, and recipient to drop off or receive goods.

“Our Appointment Delivery service helps quick commerce and modern trade suppliers meet receiving schedules, reduce delays and keep goods moving efficiently,” said Aditya Shah, Executive Director, V-Trans (India) Ltd and Chief Executive Officer, V-Xpress.

According to him, the southern expansion will cover cities like Mangalore, Davangere, Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Sirsi, Bagalkot, and Devanahalli, alongside industrial zones in Harohalli, Jigani, Bidadi, and Hindupur. “The new touchpoints aim to bring pickup and delivery services closer to manufacturing and commercial hubs,” Mr. Shah added while addressing a media conference.

As a Green Channel partner to major quick commerce platforms, V-Xpress manages B2B cargo around pre-agreed dates and confirmed warehouse receiving slots, the firm claimed. It also serves modern trade, retail chains, and Canteen Stores Department (CSD) locations.

Currently, V-Xpress supports these operations through over 40 dedicated centres offering 50,000 sq. ft. of combined storage space. The company handles roughly 10,000 tonnes of appointment-based deliveries monthly and aims to double this volume within the next year.

To improve operational efficiency, V-Xpress uses GPS tracking and electronic proof of delivery (e-POD), with partner platform API integrations nearing completion. Alongside its corporate logistics, the company is also promoting its door-to-door Box-N-Ship service to help students and individuals relocate personal belongings.

articles.title: Media access order puts MG University on collision course with Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Calling the order undemocratic, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John said that restricting media access to a public institution would undermine transparency and the public’s right to know

A face-off is brewing at Mahatma Gandhi (MG) University over media access to the campus, with Higher Education Minister Roji M. articles.title: BJP-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation denies permission for cultural event at Manaveeyam Veedhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Activists say permission for a cultural programme at Manaveeyam Veedhi featuring singer Pushpavathy was sought well in advance on November 3. They accuse the Mayor of curbing freedom of expression.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation has denied permission for a cultural programme at Manaveeyam Veedhi featuring singer Pushpavathy as part of the silver jubilee celebrations of the capital’s cultural corridor on Saturday. A collective of cultural activists who have been active at Manaveeyam since its inception accused Mayor V.V. Rajesh of attempting to curtail freedom of expression.

Veteran theatre artist D. Raghoothaman, who submitted the application for permission, told The Hindu on Friday that the collective had submitted the application for permission at the Corporation well in advance on November 3.

“Never in the past has anyone been denied permission for organising programmes at Manaveeyam. The procedure for permission was introduced only a few years ago after the street was renovated under the Smart City project. Even so, the process was only a mere formality. However, now the Mayor has started rejecting applications arbitrarily. Corporation officials had earlier informed us that no other programmes are scheduled and that the file had reached the Secretary’s desk. We had made all arrangements expecting permission, but now we are forced to cancel it because the Museum police will not give us permission to use microphone unless the Corporation clears the event,” he said.

The simmering issues at Manaveeyam Veedhi came out into the open on October 16 when the Museum Police attempted to seize a microphone ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Later, the Corporation made clear its intent to make the Street “protest-free” and to keep it limited to cultural activities, leading to protests by cultural activists who have been part of the street’s activities for a long time. CPI(M) leaders have maintained that the Manaveeyam Veedhi is a road under the Public Works department (PWD) and that its management rights have never been transferred to the Municipal Corporation.

Cultural activists at Manaveeyam are now planning to submit a memorandum to the State government to renotify the street as under the control of the Culture department, removing the Corporation from the equation.

“Manaveeyam is the only place in the city where artists or activists from economically backward or marginalised sections can make their voices heard without paying exorbitant fees to take a hall or space on rent. But now with the Corporation clamping down even on cultural programmes here, we will be left with no space to go to. Such moves will be resisted,” said Mr. Ragoothaman.

articles.title: PWD gets ₹2.68 crore to fortify three rehabilitation sites for Vallarpadam project evictees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The amount has been credited to the official bank account of the PWD Executive Engineer from the funds deposited by the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) in the district collector’s account for the rehabilitation of the evicted families

The Public Works Department (PWD) has been allotted ₹2.68 crore for the fortification of three marshy rehabilitation sites allocated to families evicted in 2008 for the rail and road connectivity projects of the Vallarpadam International Container Transhipment Terminal, thus fulfilling a longstanding demand of the affected families to make the sites habitable.

The amount has been credited to the official bank account of the PWD Executive Engineer from the funds deposited by the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) in the district collector’s account for the rehabilitation of the evicted families.

Work will begin as soon as the tendering process is completed. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee hailed the proactive intervention of District Collector G. Priyanka in finally resolving a vexed issue that had remained unresolved for nearly two decades.

This comes close on the heels of the Cochin Port Authority’s decision to release, free of cost, 52,958.70 cubic metres of dredged sand currently stocked at Puthuvypeen for fortifying the rehabilitation sites. The sites at Mulavukad, allotted to 14 families, and Adarsh Nagar and Indira Nagar at Thuthiyoor near Kakkanad, allotted to 56 and 118 families, respectively, are in need of fortification to support construction activities.

A meeting of the committee, chaired by the district collector to monitor the implementation of the rehabilitation package on October 31, entrusted the PWD with coordinating the fortification works. The funds allocated will be used for transporting the sand and carrying out the actual fortification of the rehabilitation sites. Kochi Metro Rail Limited will supervise the effectiveness of the fortification works

As many as 316 families were evicted in 2008 from Mulavukad, Moolamppilly, Kothad, Cheranalloor, Eloor, Manjummal, West Kadungalloor, Elamakkara, Ponekkara and Vaduthala without any immediate rehabilitation proposals. The rehabilitation package was notified in March that year following strong public protests.

A government order issued by the then Principal Secretary (Revenue) on March 19, 2008, in connection with the rehabilitation package, had also promised employment to one person from each evicted family, based on educational qualifications. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee had submitted a memorandum on the matter to Higher Education Minister Rojy M. John, who is also the Minister in charge of the district.

The Public Works Department (PWD) has been allotted ₹2.68 crore for the fortification of three marshy rehabilitation sites allocated to families evicted in 2008 for the rail and road connectivity projects of the Vallarpadam International Container Transhipment Terminal, thus fulfilling a longstanding demand of the affected families to make the sites habitable.

The amount has been credited to the official bank account of the PWD Executive Engineer from the funds deposited by the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) in the district collector’s account for the rehabilitation of the evicted families.

Work will begin as soon as the tendering process is completed. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee hailed the proactive intervention of District Collector G. Priyanka in finally resolving a vexed issue that had remained unresolved for nearly two decades.

This comes close on the heels of the Cochin Port Authority’s decision to release, free of cost, 52,958.70 cubic metres of dredged sand currently stocked at Puthuvypeen for fortifying the rehabilitation sites. The sites at Mulavukad, allotted to 14 families, and Adarsh Nagar and Indira Nagar at Thuthiyoor near Kakkanad, allotted to 56 and 118 families, respectively, are in need of fortification to support construction activities.

A meeting of the committee, chaired by the district collector to monitor the implementation of the rehabilitation package on October 31, entrusted the PWD with coordinating the fortification works. The funds allocated will be used for transporting the sand and carrying out the actual fortification of the rehabilitation sites. Kochi Metro Rail Limited will supervise the effectiveness of the fortification works

As many as 316 families were evicted in 2008 from Mulavukad, Moolamppilly, Kothad, Cheranalloor, Eloor, Manjummal, West Kadungalloor, Elamakkara, Ponekkara and Vaduthala without any immediate rehabilitation proposals. The rehabilitation package was notified in March that year following strong public protests.

A government order issued by the then Principal Secretary (Revenue) on March 19, 2008, in connection with the rehabilitation package, had also promised employment to one person from each evicted family, based on educational qualifications. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee had submitted a memorandum on the matter to Higher Education Minister Rojy M. John, who is also the Minister in charge of the district.

3. articles.title: Two booked for forcing Jharkhand Congress MLA’s minor domestic help to level ‘false’ rape charges against him

fullParagraphs: The girl told reporters that she was brought to Ranchi by the MLA's family in May on the promise of being enrolled in a school, but was instead made to do domestic work at his official residence

Hours after an FIR was registered against Congress MLA Bhushan Bara on the charge of raping his minor domestic help, police said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that they booked two persons for allegedly abducting and coercing the girl into making a “false" statement against the legislator.
The Congress is a constituent of the state's ruling JMM -led coalition.

“The girl's grandfather lodged a complaint at Patratanr police station in Simdega district on Friday (November 13), naming two men who allegedly abducted the 15-year-old girl three days ago and pressured her into making a false statement of rape against the two-time MLA,” Simdega SP Shrikant S. Khotre said.
“We have booked both the accused under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act,” Mr. Khotre told PTI .
One of the two men is a content creator associated with a YouTube channel.
The police officer said the case is being investigated and further action would be taken based on the evidence gathered against the accused.

The girl, a resident of Simdega district, had alleged that Mr. Bara had raped her at his residence on August 5, following which she became pregnant. She also claimed that she later learnt during a medical examination that she suffered a miscarriage.
The girl told reporters that she was brought to Ranchi by the MLA's family in May on the promise of being enrolled in a school, but was instead made to do domestic work at his official residence.
Following this, the police registered an FIR against the legislator under the POCSO Act and the Juvenile Justice Act at the Dhurwa police station in Ranchi.
Mr. Bara, a two-term MLA, denied the allegations on Friday, calling them "completely false and misleading".

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.

1. Core Context & Background: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%

India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

fullParagraphs: It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan

India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly draft resolution that reaffirms the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources and demands that Israel cease the exploitation and damage of these resources.

The 193-Member UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in favour of the resolution ‘Permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and of the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources’ proposed by Uruguay.

It stressed that the wall and settlements being constructed by Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including in and around East Jerusalem, are contrary to international law and seriously deprive the Palestinian people of their natural resources.
It also called for full compliance with the legal obligations affirmed in the July 2004 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice and relevant UN resolutions.

The resolution called upon Israel to comply strictly with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and immediately and completely cease all policies and measures aimed at altering the character and status of the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.

It further called upon Israel to halt all actions, including those perpetrated by Israeli settlers, that harm the environment, including the dumping of waste materials in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and the occupied Syrian Golan.

It also called upon Israel to cease its destruction of vital infrastructure, including water pipelines, sewage networks and electricity networks, and to cease its demolition and confiscation of Palestinian homes and civilian infrastructure, agricultural lands and water wells.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.
The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.

The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

articles.title: No locus standi: Indian envoy hits back at USCIRF for remarks on Sharjeel Imam
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X, describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”

Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra has asked an American advisory body to introspect on its own prejudices and stop lecturing others, after the bipartisan agency flagged arrests in India allegedly on religious grounds.

Mr. Kwatra’s sharp retort on Friday (November 13, 2026) came after the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X , describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”.

Former Jawaharlal Nehru University scholar Imam has been booked under UAPA (Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act) on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.
The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.
“USCIRF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens,” Kwatra said
“Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths,” he said.

He said India flourishes, defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. “Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others,” Mr. Kwatra said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

articles.title: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Continuous glucose monitors and automated insulin delivery systems drastically improve glycaemic control and cut hospitalisations, yet steep out-of-pocket costs and socioeconomic disparities leave a massive adoption gap

Diabetes management is moving beyond periodic finger-prick tests and clinic visits, with technologies such as continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps and mobile applications providing more detailed information on glucose levels and helping patients make day-to-day decisions about their care.

CGMs use a sensor placed on the arm or abdomen to measure glucose levels at regular intervals, offering a picture of fluctuations through the day and night. Insulin pumps deliver insulin continuously, while automated insulin delivery systems combine CGM readings with algorithms to adjust insulin delivery. Mobile applications can bring together information on glucose levels, food intake, physical activity and medication.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Samsung announces Google co-developed pricing and sale details of its smart glasses
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Equipped with a high-definition camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them

Samsung has officially unveiled its new lineup of intelligent eyewear , bringing hands-free artificial intelligence into everyday fashion. Developed in partnership with Google, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the smart glasses integrate Google’s Gemini AI directly into stylish frames built for daily wear.

Set to launch on December 10, 2026, in the U.S. and South Korea, with pre-orders starting today, the collection features 30 distinct frame styles. Weighing around 41 grams, the frames combine Warby Parker’s classic look with Gentle Monster’s bold design aesthetics.

The smart glasses run on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform. Equipped with a 12 MP HD camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them. Wearers can ask Gemini to identify objects and landmarks, translate menus instantly or follow step-by-step navigation via Google Maps.

For workplace efficiency, the glasses can capture meeting whiteboards, generate key summaries and automatically sync them into Samsung Notes. The system also organises, summarises, and reads aloud incoming notifications.

To address privacy concerns, the eyewear design includes visible recording lights and audio chimes whenever the camera captures images or video. Additionally, the software claims to automatically blur bystanders’ faces during visual queries, while open-ear speakers are tuned to limit sound leakage.
The eyewear claims up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, extending up to 72 hours with its charging case.
The U.S. pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models, while Gentle Monster frames range from $449 to $489.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Starship expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for ​Saturday afternoon; the Super Heavy booster was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) on a mission the company hopes will ‌be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, ​a key test of Elon Musk’s effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship’s uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter ⁠the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and “chopstick”-arm technology to recover Starship’s lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within ‌minutes of the launch. But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface.
The booster for SpaceX's mega rocket Starship explodes after a catch attempt was aborted during a test flight from Starbase, Texas. | Photo Credit: AP

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship’s upper stage back to home base at the ‌end ⁠of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

Bringing the top portion ⁠of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its ​launch pad from SpaceX’s South Texas Starbase complex along the ‌Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship’s 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX’s satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take ‌less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk’s space and AI business ​views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
“We have no indication that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services,” Microsoft said in an update on social media.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.
