📰 Caste and class: On OBC reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Librarian P.V. Konnur felicitated on his 75th birth anniversary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Friends, colleagues and admirers of P.V. Konnur, the library science professional and president of LIS Academy, Bengaluru, felicitated him on his 75th birth anniversary.
The Amruta Mahotsava was held at the Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University on Thursday.

Ramesh B., Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, released the felicitation volume brought out in Prof. Konnur’s honour and he said that such a dedicated librarian is very hard to find today, and that Prof. Konnur is a role model for budding librarians.

He observed that the librarian’s role has become more challenging, as students now have to be drawn back to libraries from their mobile phones. He urged Prof. Konnur to lead this movement and to help university libraries become experiential centres.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: AIADMK leader accuses govt. of seeking to mislead people on clearances of industrial projects without being aware of the systems in existence

The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Friday (November 13, 2026) criticised the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government saying it was seeking to mislead people on clearances of industrial projects without being aware of the systems in existence.

In a statement, Mr. Palaniswami referred to the reported observation of Industries Minister S. Keerthana regarding the proposed scheme of providing clearances in 21 days and recalled that when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister in 2014, she unveiled the system of giving the approvals in 30 days. Subsequently, when he was in power, the nods were issued for many industrial projects.

The AIADMK leader reiterated his criticism of the TVK-led regime of missing opportunities with regard to industrial investments, just as in the areas of law and order, women’s security and drug abuse.

Referring to a series of recent incidents of crime such as a major gold heist in Madurai and robbery of ₹1.5 crore in various outlets of the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation in Kancheepuram district, Mr. Palaniswami stated that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had still remained in “state of silence,” even as the people were in the “grip of fear.”

In another post, the AIADMK leader came down heavily on the State government’s celebration of Children’s Day and wondered whether there was “no sense of shame” on the part of the Chief Minister when the incidence of violence against women and children was “on the rise” in the TVK-led reign. He called upon the government to bring to book those responsible for the incidents of crime against the children.

Mr. Palaniswami announced that the women’s wing of his party would hold a demonstration in Kallakurichi on November 17 (Tuesday) to highlight the government’s “failure” in taking action against the ruling party’s Kallakurichi legislator who had allegedly sent an inappropriate message to District Collector J.E. Padmaja

The Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran adverted to reports of women functionaries of the ruling party complaining about their treatment by their men colleagues in the organisation in Tiruvannamalai and Coimbatore districts and asked Mr Vijay, who had once declared that there would be “no compromise on incidents of violence against women,” whether he would take steps against those concerned.

articles.title: Former MIDS Director P.G. Babu no more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies, passed away in Dindigul, his hometown, on Thursday. He was 65 and is survived by his mother, a brother, and a sister.

Prof. Babu was serving as the Vice-Chancellor of Vidyashilp University, Bengaluru, since 2023. During his tenure as the Director of MIDS between 2019 and 2022, he brought out a series of books in both Tamil and English, most notably on the economic policy during the pandemic.
For over three decades, he had served at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, Mumbai, where he was also the Dean of Graduate Studies and coordinated the Law and Economics programmes.

His research focussed on Microeconomic theory and Game theory with applications across Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Law and Economics, and Politics-Philosophy and Economics. His research contributions include work on the decision-making framework for climate change as part of the IPCC working group, which earned him a citation from the Prime Minister of India.

articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Disruption to Microsoft’s cloud-based email service affects business operations and airline customer support in India; public services in several countries also report problems

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

articles.title: After CBI, ED arrests Mahadev betting app scam accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “In ED custody, Saurabh Chandrakar will be confronted with the statements of his associates, digital data and documents concerning his foreign entities and evidence of commission of offence of money laundering,” an ED official said

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Friday (November 13, 2026) said it has arrested Saurabh Chandrakar, co-owner and promoter of the Mahadev Online Book illegal betting syndicate, and would now be confronting with the evidence of money laundering against him.

Earlier on Thursday (November 12, 2026), a special CBI court remanded Chandrakar to seven days’ judicial custody and dismissed ED’s application to execute their non-bailable warrant against him. On Friday (November 13, 2026) post the arrest, the ED produced him at a special PMLA [Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002] court in Raipur which remanded him to ED custody for seven days till November 19 for further investigation.

“In ED custody, Saurabh Chandrakar will be confronted with the statements of his associates, digital data and documents concerning his foreign entities and evidence of commission of offence of money laundering,” an ED official said.

According to the ED, Chandrakar and another co-promoter Ravi Uppal operated “Mahadev Online Book” (various online betting websites) from Head Office in Dubai through a franchise of “betting panels” across India and the United Arab Emirates.

A statement further noted that player money went through bank accounts held in other people’s names and left India through hawala. ED’s main complaint of October 2023 estimated the syndicate’s earnings at about ₹450 crore a month.

“Saurabh Chandrakar did not answer the summons issued to him by ED in September 2023 and continued to evade investigation by law enforcement agencies. On ED’s application, the Special Court issued a Non-Bailable Warrant against him on 04.09.2023, and shortly thereafter, INTERPOL also published a Red Notice against him on ED’s request. His challenge to the warrant was dismissed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh on 22.03.2025. He obtained a passport of Vanuatu while holding an Indian passport, and even claimed before the Special Court that he had given up Indian citizenship on 28.06.2022,” the official said.

On the progress of the investigations into money laundering allegations, the official said that the ED had thus far searched about 190 premises, seized or frozen about ₹2,000 crore and attached property now valued at about ₹3,500 crore, about ₹1,800 crore of it abroad, including 22 immovable properties in Dubai. It has filed six prosecution complaints against 116 accused. Saurabh Chandrakar is the fifteenth person arrested by ED in this case, the ED statement noted.

The agency purportedly followed the money from panel operators through the Dubai Head Office to hawala handlers and share-market investors. “It froze securities of about ₹236 crore held by Dubai companies in September 2023. In July 2026 ED arrested Vikas Garg, whose companies received about ₹940 crore of betting proceeds, of which about ₹766 crore went into the acquisition of the United States company Ebix Inc. ED has attached about ₹941 crore in that limb,” the official said.

The ED statement also mentioned Chandrakar’s lavish wedding in UAE in the year 2023. “The wedding at Ras Al Khaimah in February 2023 cost about ₹200 crore in cash, with three chartered aircraft from Nagpur. ED traced that money through the event company, hotels and angadia firms, and the guest list it recovered identified the management of the syndicate,” the official added.

articles.title: Two-year-old dies after firecracker explodes inside his mouth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The victim parents said that the boy put a pop-pop firecracker in his mouth while playing, which exploded, injuring his gums and causing bleeding

articles.title: File FIR against those who tarnish party’s image says Bengal BJP chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “BJP has reached here (came to power) by keeping them out. BJP has no need to touch them,” West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said, adding that doors of the party are closed for outsiders.

Observing that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power without the support of those trying to make into the party now, president of the party’s West Bengal unit Samik Bhattacharya on Friday (November 13, 2026) said that FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish the image of the party.

“Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers, I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said. The remarks made by the Bengal BJP chief have been made at a time when there are allegations that leaders and supporters of other parties are trying to join the BJP. There have been certain reports of BJP supporters allegedly indulging in extortion after the party came to power, a charge that was levelled against Trinamool Congress leaders when the party was in power. “BJP has reached here (came to power) by keeping them out. BJP has no need to touch them,” he said.

Mr. Bhattacharya said that there can be some ‘deviations’ and the “party will correct them”. The BJP leader said anyone cannot claim allegiance to the party simply by garlanding BJP leaders. “The door was closed before; it is still closed. The door has not been officially opened,” he said. The remarks by the Bengal BJP chief come amidst claims that it is facing a challenge of “Trinamoolisation of the BJP” and Mr. Bhattacharya has been saying that the party will resist it.

While the BJP president warned against outsiders getting into the party, he made it clear that it will be BJP leaders who are appointed as ward commissioners. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the party will not take suggestions from Md. Salim, the CPI(M) State secretary or any other party to appoint coordinators to oversee civic services in Kolkata and Howrah if municipal elections were delayed.

“They (the ward coordinators) will be BJP people,” he said. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had said that the government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court.

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

articles.title: NHRC seeks Education Ministry’s response over alleged neglect of Veer Baal Diwas in schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The NHRC acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday sought an explanation from the Union Ministry of Education over allegations that schools across the country give greater prominence to Children’s Day celebrations on November 14 while failing to adequately highlight the historical significance of Veer Baal Diwas, observed on December 26.

The Commission’s bench, headed by member Priyank Kanoongo, acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh.

The Commission hence issued a notice to the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India asking whether the Central Government or any competent authority has issued an official notification, order or circular declaring November 14 as Children’s Day. If such a directive exists, the Ministry has been asked to furnish a copy and provide the relevant details.
The Ministry has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within 14 days, addressing the concerns raised in the complaint.

The NHRC has also sought clarification on whether schools are being encouraged to conduct dedicated educational and awareness programmes on December 26 to commemorate Veer Baal Diwas. Such initiatives, the Commission has indicated, should help students understand the historical significance of the four Sahibzadas and their extraordinary courage and sacrifice.

Highlighting the broader educational implications of the issue, the Commission stressed the need to ensure that children are exposed to important chapters of India’s history and cultural heritage. It observed that educational institutions play a significant role in nurturing awareness of values such as bravery, faith, sacrifice and resistance to injustice.

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday sought an explanation from the Union Ministry of Education over allegations that schools across the country give greater prominence to Children’s Day celebrations on November 14 while failing to adequately highlight the historical significance of Veer Baal Diwas, observed on December 26.

The Commission’s bench, headed by member Priyank Kanoongo, acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh.

The Commission hence issued a notice to the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India asking whether the Central Government or any competent authority has issued an official notification, order or circular declaring November 14 as Children’s Day. If such a directive exists, the Ministry has been asked to furnish a copy and provide the relevant details.

The Ministry has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within 14 days, addressing the concerns raised in the complaint.

The NHRC has also sought clarification on whether schools are being encouraged to conduct dedicated educational and awareness programmes on December 26 to commemorate Veer Baal Diwas. Such initiatives, the Commission has indicated, should help students understand the historical significance of the four Sahibzadas and their extraordinary courage and sacrifice.

Highlighting the broader educational implications of the issue, the Commission stressed the need to ensure that children are exposed to important chapters of India’s history and cultural heritage. It observed that educational institutions play a significant role in nurturing awareness of values such as bravery, faith, sacrifice and resistance to injustice.

articles.title: The challenge of holding the Quad together
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The big ticket question confronting the Quad, however, is how Donald Trump engages with the group and the broader Indo-Pacific geography

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the U.S. Secretary of State announced that the leaders of the four Quad countries — India, Australia, Japan and the U.S. — are expected to meet in Manila in November, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. The announcement is significant, as this would be the first summit-level meeting of the Quad leaders since Donald Trump began his second term as U.S. President. It would also be the first such summit attended by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi since she assumed office. The last Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

While India was expected to host the subsequent Quad Leaders’ Summit, the grouping underwent a period of intense strategic turbulence in 2025, on account of Washington’s shifting geopolitical priorities and changing political dynamics in its bilateral relations with Quad members, especially India. However, this did not result in complete collapse of the grouping. Apart from the leader-level summit, the group has remained successful in continuing its operational synergies in its various initiatives. This was most evident in the elevation of the Quad’s Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness initiative to the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration framework, launched in New Delhi in May 2026, following the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
Political & National Report: The challenge of holding the Quad together. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: All departing U.S. flights grounded due to communication outage
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks; Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the country and “this isn’t another 9/11”

All flights in the U.S. were grounded on Friday (November 13, 2026), sparking travel chaos across the vast country, after what government officials said was a major communications outage, insisting it was not the result of any “nefarious attack.”
The nationwide stop left tens of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.
The incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks.
“So supposedly, nobody’s flying, but they haven’t told the public yet,” said an exasperated Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.
“We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.”

The Federal Aviation Administration “issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centres,” the agency said. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”
In a subsequent message on X, the agency described the problem as “a temporary telecommunications outage” and said it was acting “out of an abundance of caution.”
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the United States.

“There was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us, it’s just a telecommunication outage, as of right now,” Mr. Mullin said, adding officials were “not ruling out anything at this point.”

The Federal Aviation Administration “issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centres,” the agency said. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the United States.

“There was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us, it’s just a telecommunication outage, as of right now,” Mr. Mullin said, adding officials were “not ruling out anything at this point.”

articles.title: Tanker hits a river cruise boat on Mississippi River in New Orleans; rescue operations under way
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over; ‘miracle on the Mississippi”, says New Orleans Mayor

A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard on Friday (November 13, 2026), the Mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over.
Video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the cruise boat while it was docked as metal and glass crashed and crunched.
Tugboat operators, nearby workers, police and several other rescuers rushed to help. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno called it “a miracle on the Mississippi.”
The Mayor said 32 people were taken to the hospital, but none of them had critical injuries.
The boat started listing within minutes and flipped while emergency workers were still trying to get everyone off the ship.
Dozens of people on board and at least two police officers were dragged from the 19°C river onto nearby ships.
Devon Flanagan was at his job nearby at the Port of New Orleans when workers rushed down the dock. He got out of his truck and saw the American Heritage on its side and passengers in the water.

“It was just chaos,” he said. “You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water.”
The cruise ship was built in 2015 and operated by American Cruise Lines. It is five stories and can hold up to 150 passengers.
The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: No ETA yet on full recovery, company says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
“We have no indication that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services,” Microsoft said in an update on social media.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.

articles.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NPPA directs State drug controllers to strictly monitor prices
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs

The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%.

Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said.

All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites.

The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients.
Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted.

Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

1. Core Context & Background: NPPA directs State drug controllers to strictly monitor prices

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

He has also been summoned by Girish Park police station in the city on November 20 in connection with another social media post.

articles.title: V-Xpress building key logistics hubs in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under Southern expansion, the company will cover cities like Mangalore, Davangere, Gulbarga, Bijapur, Sirsi, Bagalkot, and Devanahalli, alongside industrial zones in Harohalli, Jigani, Bidadi, and Hindupur

V-Xpress, the Mumbai-headquartered express cargo arm of V-Trans (India) Ltd, is sharpening its focus on South India, targeting key hubs, including Bengaluru and the industrial clusters of Narasapura and Dabaspet, as it expands its services in the region.

The logistics firm said it would open more than 15 new outlets across Karnataka, a move expected to generate over 150 local jobs and focus on Appointment Delivery service for the quick commerce and organised retail sectors. An appointment delivery is a pre-arranged date and time slot agreed upon by the shipper, carrier, and recipient to drop off or receive goods.

“Our Appointment Delivery service helps quick commerce and modern trade suppliers meet receiving schedules, reduce delays and keep goods moving efficiently,” said Aditya Shah, Executive Director, V-Trans (India) Ltd and Chief Executive Officer, V-Xpress.

According to him, the southern expansion will cover cities like Mangalore, Davangere, Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Sirsi, Bagalkot, and Devanahalli, alongside industrial zones in Harohalli, Jigani, Bidadi, and Hindupur. “The new touchpoints aim to bring pickup and delivery services closer to manufacturing and commercial hubs,” Mr. Shah added while addressing a media conference.

As a Green Channel partner to major quick commerce platforms, V-Xpress manages B2B cargo around pre-agreed dates and confirmed warehouse receiving slots, the firm claimed. It also serves modern trade, retail chains, and Canteen Stores Department (CSD) locations.

Currently, V-Xpress supports these operations through over 40 dedicated centres offering 50,000 sq. ft. of combined storage space. The company handles roughly 10,000 tonnes of appointment-based deliveries monthly and aims to double this volume within the next year.

To improve operational efficiency, V-Xpress uses GPS tracking and electronic proof of delivery (e-POD), with partner platform API integrations nearing completion. Alongside its corporate logistics, the company is also promoting its door-to-door Box-N-Ship service to help students and individuals relocate personal belongings.

articles.title: Media access order puts MG University on collision course with Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Calling the order undemocratic, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John said that restricting media access to a public institution would undermine transparency and the public’s right to know

A face-off is brewing at Mahatma Gandhi (MG) University over media access to the campus, with Higher Education Minister Roji M. John demanding the immediate withdrawal of an order requiring journalists to obtain the Vice-Chancellor’s prior permission before entering the campus to gather university-related news. But the university is refusing to back down, insisting that the directive is merely an administrative arrangement and not a ban on the media.

Calling the order undemocratic, Mr. John said that restricting media access to a public institution would undermine transparency and the public’s right to know. He warned that any attempt to curb media freedom would be strongly resisted.

In a social media post, the Minister invoked Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, which guarantees freedom of speech and expression, and said media freedom was an integral part of it. “Universities should be spaces for free thought and democratic discourse. Restricting media access to such institutions reflects authoritarian tendencies. Any attempt to undermine media freedom will be strongly opposed,” he said, adding that the government would not allow such measures at MG University or any other higher education institution in Kerala.

The university, however, has stood its ground. “There is no ban on the media, as is being construed. This is an administrative arrangement to ensure transparent and secure entry to the campus, similar to the regulations applicable to other visitors,” Vice-Chancellor D. Mavuth told The Hindu .

Varsity sources, meanwhile, indicated that the order is unlikely to be withdrawn in response to the Minister’s demand. They maintained that the university was bound by the directions of the Governor and its Chancellor, and not those of the Minister. They also linked the move to the widening rift between the UDF-backed Syndicate members and the Vice-Chancellor, a nominee of the Governor.

articles.title: BJP-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation denies permission for cultural event at Manaveeyam Veedhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Activists say permission for a cultural programme at Manaveeyam Veedhi featuring singer Pushpavathy was sought well in advance on November 3. They accuse the Mayor of curbing freedom of expression.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation has denied permission for a cultural programme at Manaveeyam Veedhi featuring singer Pushpavathy as part of the silver jubilee celebrations of the capital’s cultural corridor on Saturday. A collective of cultural activists who have been active at Manaveeyam since its inception accused Mayor V.V. Rajesh of attempting to curtail freedom of expression.

Veteran theatre artist D. Raghoothaman, who submitted the application for permission, told The Hindu on Friday that the collective had submitted the application for permission at the Corporation well in advance on November 3.

“Never in the past has anyone been denied permission for organising programmes at Manaveeyam. The procedure for permission was introduced only a few years ago after the street was renovated under the Smart City project. Even so, the process was only a mere formality. However, now the Mayor has started rejecting applications arbitrarily. Corporation officials had earlier informed us that no other programmes are scheduled and that the file had reached the Secretary’s desk. We had made all arrangements expecting permission, but now we are forced to cancel it because the Museum police will not give us permission to use microphone unless the Corporation clears the event,” he said.

The simmering issues at Manaveeyam Veedhi came out into the open on October 16 when the Museum Police attempted to seize a microphone ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Later, the Corporation made clear its intent to make the Street “protest-free” and to keep it limited to cultural activities, leading to protests by cultural activists who have been part of the street’s activities for a long time. CPI(M) leaders have maintained that the Manaveeyam Veedhi is a road under the Public Works department (PWD) and that its management rights have never been transferred to the Municipal Corporation.

Cultural activists at Manaveeyam are now planning to submit a memorandum to the State government to renotify the street as under the control of the Culture department, removing the Corporation from the equation.

“Manaveeyam is the only place in the city where artists or activists from economically backward or marginalised sections can make their voices heard without paying exorbitant fees to take a hall or space on rent. But now with the Corporation clamping down even on cultural programmes here, we will be left with no space to go to. Such moves will be resisted,” said Mr. Ragoothaman.

articles.title: PWD gets ₹2.68 crore to fortify three rehabilitation sites for Vallarpadam project evictees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The amount has been credited to the official bank account of the PWD Executive Engineer from the funds deposited by the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) in the district collector’s account for the rehabilitation of the evicted families

The Public Works Department (PWD) has been allotted ₹2.68 crore for the fortification of three marshy rehabilitation sites allocated to families evicted in 2008 for the rail and road connectivity projects of the Vallarpadam International Container Transhipment Terminal, thus fulfilling a longstanding demand of the affected families to make the sites habitable.

The amount has been credited to the official bank account of the PWD Executive Engineer from the funds deposited by the Cochin Port Authority (CoPA) in the district collector’s account for the rehabilitation of the evicted families.

Work will begin as soon as the tendering process is completed. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee hailed the proactive intervention of District Collector G. Priyanka in finally resolving a vexed issue that had remained unresolved for nearly two decades.

This comes close on the heels of the Cochin Port Authority’s decision to release, free of cost, 52,958.70 cubic metres of dredged sand currently stocked at Puthuvypeen for fortifying the rehabilitation sites. The sites at Mulavukad, allotted to 14 families, and Adarsh Nagar and Indira Nagar at Thuthiyoor near Kakkanad, allotted to 56 and 118 families, respectively, are in need of fortification to support construction activities.

A meeting of the committee, chaired by the district collector to monitor the implementation of the rehabilitation package on October 31, entrusted the PWD with coordinating the fortification works. The funds allocated will be used for transporting the sand and carrying out the actual fortification of the rehabilitation sites. Kochi Metro Rail Limited will supervise the effectiveness of the fortification works

As many as 316 families were evicted in 2008 from Mulavukad, Moolamppilly, Kothad, Cheranalloor, Eloor, Manjummal, West Kadungalloor, Elamakkara, Ponekkara and Vaduthala without any immediate rehabilitation proposals. The rehabilitation package was notified in March that year following strong public protests.

A government order issued by the then Principal Secretary (Revenue) on March 19, 2008, in connection with the rehabilitation package, had also promised employment to one person from each evicted family, based on educational qualifications. The Moolamppilly Coordination Committee had submitted a memorandum on the matter to Higher Education Minister Rojy M. John, who is also the Minister in charge of the district.

articles.title: India supports UNGA resolution on permanent sovereignty of Palestinian people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan

India has voted in favour of a UN General Assembly draft resolution that reaffirms the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources and demands that Israel cease the exploitation and damage of these resources.

The 193-Member UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in favour of the resolution ‘Permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and of the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources’ proposed by Uruguay.
India voted in favour of the resolution along with 150 other UN Member States, while Israel and the U.S. were among the seven nations that voted against the draft, which got 11 abstentions.
The resolution reaffirmed the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and of the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources, including land, water and energy resources.

It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan.

It stressed that the wall and settlements being constructed by Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including in and around East Jerusalem, are contrary to international law and seriously deprive the Palestinian people of their natural resources.
It also called for full compliance with the legal obligations affirmed in the July 2004 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice and relevant UN resolutions.

The resolution called upon Israel to comply strictly with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and immediately and completely cease all policies and measures aimed at altering the character and status of the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.

It further called upon Israel to halt all actions, including those perpetrated by Israeli settlers, that harm the environment, including the dumping of waste materials in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and the occupied Syrian Golan.

It also called upon Israel to cease its destruction of vital infrastructure, including water pipelines, sewage networks and electricity networks, and to cease its demolition and confiscation of Palestinian homes and civilian infrastructure, agricultural lands and water wells.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.
The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.

articles.title: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say

fullParagraphs: Continuous glucose monitors and automated insulin delivery systems drastically improve glycaemic control and cut hospitalisations, yet steep out-of-pocket costs and socioeconomic disparities leave a massive adoption gap

Diabetes management is moving beyond periodic finger-prick tests and clinic visits, with technologies such as continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps and mobile applications providing more detailed information on glucose levels and helping patients make day-to-day decisions about their care.

CGMs use a sensor placed on the arm or abdomen to measure glucose levels at regular intervals, offering a picture of fluctuations through the day and night. Insulin pumps deliver insulin continuously, while automated insulin delivery systems combine CGM readings with algorithms to adjust insulin delivery. Mobile applications can bring together information on glucose levels, food intake, physical activity and medication.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Starship expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for ​Saturday afternoon; the Super Heavy booster was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) on a mission the company hopes will ‌be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, ​a key test of Elon Musk’s effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship’s uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter ⁠the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and “chopstick”-arm technology to recover Starship’s lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within ‌minutes of the launch. But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface.
The booster for SpaceX's mega rocket Starship explodes after a catch attempt was aborted during a test flight from Starbase, Texas. | Photo Credit: AP

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship’s upper stage back to home base at the ‌end ⁠of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

Bringing the top portion ⁠of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its ​launch pad from SpaceX’s South Texas Starbase complex along the ‌Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship’s 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX’s satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take ‌less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk’s space and AI business ​views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
“We have no indication that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services,” Microsoft said in an update on social media.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Without peace, Israel risks descending into chaos

Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.
Editorial Context: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: Restrictions on me arbitrary, vague: Sonam Wangchuk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ladakh administration shifted the activist from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence

Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday (November 12, 2026) described the restrictions imposed by the administration on him as “bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate” and conspicuously “not using words such as house arrest”.

Invoking Section 163(1) of the BNSS, the Ladakh administration on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) evening shifted Mr. Wangchuk from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence.

“I was driven towards my village, where my residence is and was eventually taken to HIAL, reaching there at approximately 8.40 p.m. [on Wednesday]. I was told to remain at home under the supervision of police guards. Since that evening, dozens of armed police personnel [approximately 20 to 22] have been stationed at and around my residence,” said Mr. Wangchuk in a letter to senior officials of Ladakh and the Union Home Ministry.

Referring to the order issued by the Additional District Magistrate, Leh, Mr. Wangchuk said it disclosed no reasons justifying the necessity or proportionality of such an extended restriction, nor does it identify any continuing emergency or threat attributable to me that would warrant restraints of such duration.”

“The actions have clearly been taken to curtail my movement and rights before the election. The order is clearly bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate. I request you to kindly offer the clarification at the earliest, and withdraw this order without delay,” said Mr. Wangchuk, in the letter.
He claimed there was “no explicit order of house arrest or directing deployment of police personnel was shown to me then, and none has been served on me since”.

“I have not sought any security cover, and I am not aware of any threat to my person. No written order authorising this deployment has been furnished to me, and I do not know who directed it, on what date, or under what provision of law. I would be grateful to be informed of these particulars,” he added.

The Ladakh activist, who was arrested in September last year under the National Security Act (NSA) and released in March this year, said the Ladakh administration’s order “conspicuously does not use words such as “house arrest”.

“It does not use the words “detention” or “confinement”. It nowhere directs me to remain at my residence — a direction given orally to me by the personnel who picked me up and are now present outside my house. The order does not mention the scope or extent of the restrictions imposed on my movement, leaving their implementation to the discretion of the police personnel deployed,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

The alleged restrictions on Mr. Wanghuk came when Ladakh was preparing to hold polls for panchayat and municipality on November 21 and for hill councils on December 4. However, Ladakh’s key civil society bodies, Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), have organised protests and demanded postponement of council elections to April-May next year.

articles.title: Palaniswami rejects speculation of Dhinakaran, Sasikala being readmitted into AIADMK
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Thursday termed as “unnecessary” a question about the possibility of readmitting AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran and former interim general secretary of the AIADMK V.K. Sasikala into the AIADMK.

“Please understand that they [Mr. Dhinakaran and Ms. Sasikala] have started their own parties. Please ask better questions,” Mr. Palaniswami said during an interaction with journalists at the Chennai airport.
