articles.title: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as U.S.-led talks consider wider European security
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Kyiv's forces are using drones and ground robots to help defend against Russia's army along the about 1,200-km front line snaking down eastern and southeastern Ukraine
Ukraine fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow's invasion nearly five years ago.

Meanwhile, negotiators raised the stakes in talks to stop the fighting by including for discussion wider European security arrangements that have been in place since the end of the Cold War. That has alarmed European leaders and placed a question mark over NATO's future role.

After two days of talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi this week, U.S. envoys went in person to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was meeting with European Union leaders in Dublin, Ireland.
Further talks are planned as negotiators seek a breakthrough in peace efforts, according to U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also President Donald Trump's son-in-law.
Mr. Kushner said Russia has agreed to include Europe in upcoming talks, after Moscow's long insistence that the continent's governments were part of the problem because they were supporting Ukraine.

Europe's presence at the negotiating table will allow negotiators “to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Mr. Kushner said on X.
As European leaders scrambled to find an envoy to the talks, they were also wary of Russian maneuvering as well as Mr. Trump's praise for Mr. Putin and his administration's sharp criticism of Europe.
The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said on Friday (November 13, 2026) that Europe must insist on a ceasefire before taking the negotiations further — the opposite of what Mr. Putin demands.
“If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us,” she said in Dublin.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden insisted that Europe must take its fate into its own hands.

articles.title: Syria removes visa restrictions on U.S. travellers after backlash
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The current Syrian government, in place since Islamist-led fighters overthrew Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, has allowed Westerners to obtain entry visas at Damascus airport or border crossings
Syria has lifted restrictions on the entry of U.S. citizens imposed several days ago, an official told AFP on Friday (November 13, 2026), after the limits sparked uproar online.
The current Syrian government, in place since Islamist-led fighters overthrew Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, has allowed Westerners to obtain entry visas at Damascus airport or border crossings.
However, this week, several U.S. citizens complained on social media that they had been turned away on the grounds they needed a visa in advance.

"The entry procedures for U.S. citizens travelling to Syria have returned to their earlier state, after the cancellation of the obligation to obtain prior authorisation, which was imposed temporarily by the interior ministry," Mazen Allouch, an official with the ports and borders authority, told AFP .
He said there had been no change for citizens of other countries, including Europeans.

According to Syria's Tourism Ministry, 719,000 tourists, excluding travellers from Arab nations, visited the country in the first six months of 2026, despite its struggles to recover from more than a decade of civil war and the sectarian and ethnic tensions that followed its end.
That figure was a sharp increase on the number from 2025, which was just 131,000.
International flights have resumed to Syria, while Western nations including the United States have lifted sanctions imposed on Damascus during the Assad years in an effort to help it rebuild.

articles.title: Eisenkot urges respect for Israel's Arab minority after Netanyahu attacks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month's election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Eisenkot to form a government

Israeli Prime Ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot called on Friday (November 13, 2026) for respect for the country's Arab minority after caretaker Premier Benjamin Netanyahu and other right-wing figures sought to delegitimise the community's lawmakers by linking them to Hamas.

Two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month's election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Mr. Eisenkot to form a government.
"Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story," Mr. Eisenkot wrote on X on Friday (November 13, 2026).

fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.
The company said its teams are reviewing the incident and working to prevent similar disruptions in the future.

Microsoft says service availability is improving, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels. However, some users may continue to face intermittent access issues and delayed email delivery as the company restores affected infrastructure and monitors recovery.
Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America and across much of Europe.

articles.title: Experts call for coordinated action across sectors to tackle antimicrobial resistance
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Ahead of World AMR Awareness Week, global health experts stress the need for stronger surveillance, prevention, sustainable financing and a One Health approach to address antimicrobial resistance

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was associated with more than 4.7 million deaths in 2021, highlighting the need for coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, experts said at the sixth Global Media Forum on AMR.

Speaking ahead of World AMR Awareness Week (November 18-24), Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, Director ai-AMR Department, World Health Organization (WHO), and Director, Quadripartite Joint Secretariat on AMR, said gaps in financing, surveillance, and coordination continued to hamper global efforts. “Behind these numbers are patients, families, farmers, and communities,” he said, stressing that global commitments should translate into results on the ground.

The updated Global Action Plan on AMR for 2026-2036 seeks to strengthen prevention, surveillance, responsible antimicrobial use and sustainable financing. World leaders have committed to reducing bacterial AMR-associated deaths by 10% by 2030.

Junxia Song, deputy chief veterinarian and chief of the One Health and Disease Control Branch, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), said antibiotic use in livestock could increase by nearly 30% by 2040 without intervention. Better animal health and farm management practices could reduce use by up to 57%.

Aitziber Echeverria, AMR coordinator, Chemicals and Health Branch, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), called for action against environmental pollution, including antimicrobial residues in wastewater.

Kefas Samson, senior technical officer and lead of multisectoral coordination, AMR Department, WHO headquarters, highlighted gaps in diagnostics, surveillance and access to quality-assured antimicrobials. Jane Lwoyero, programme officer, World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), stressed the importance of vaccination and farm biosecurity.
Shobha Shukla, chairperson, Global AMR Media Alliance (GAMA), and host of the forum, called for a person-centred, rights-based and gender-transformative approach to tackling AMR.
The forum also recognised 56 journalists and media professionals as Global AMR Media Awardees 2026 for their contributions to reporting on antimicrobial resistance.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was associated with more than 4.7 million deaths in 2021, highlighting the need for coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, experts said at the sixth Global Media Forum on AMR.

Speaking ahead of World AMR Awareness Week (November 18-24), Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, Director ai-AMR Department, World Health Organization (WHO), and Director, Quadripartite Joint Secretariat on AMR, said gaps in financing, surveillance, and coordination continued to hamper global efforts. “Behind these numbers are patients, families, farmers, and communities,” he said, stressing that global commitments should translate into results on the ground.

Junxia Song, deputy chief veterinarian and chief of the One Health and Disease Control Branch, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), said antibiotic use in livestock could increase by nearly 30% by 2040 without intervention. The inquiry was subsequently adjourned after the institutions assured the Commission that their management would appear at the next hearing.

articles.title: As external funding to combat TB falls, domestic spending accounts for 86%: WHO report
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: TB cases remain one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent, with a quarter of all cases concentrated in India in 2025

Around 86% of the spending on measures against tuberculosis (TB) in 2025 came from domestic sources, the recently released Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 by the World Health Organisation (WHO) said, even as the reduction in international donor funding to combat the infectious disease remains a cause of concern.

TB cases remain one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent, with a quarter of all cases concentrated in India in 2025. The report notes that $22 billion is needed annually for TB prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care to achieve the global targets agreed on at the 2023 United Nations high-level TB meeting by 2027.

In absolute terms, Brazil, China, India, the Russian Federation, and South Africa accounted for $3.7 billion (65%) of the total of $5.63 billion provided from domestic sources in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

The report notes that international donor funding fell by 14%, from $1.1 billion in 2024 to $0.94 billion in 2025, having been relatively stable at about $1.1–1.3 billion per year between 2015 and 2024.

Financing for TB research and innovation, at $1.2 billion in 2023, also continued to fall far short of the global target of $5 billion per year. Progress to date has been constrained by the overall level of investment, said the report.

“TB mostly affects adults in their most productive years. However, all age groups are at risk. Over 80% of cases and deaths are in low- and middle-income countries. In 2025, the largest number of new TB cases occurred in the WHO South-East Asia Region (35%),’’ said the report.

The WHO on Friday (November 13, 2026) called on countries in the South-East Asia Region to accelerate action to end TB. The latest TB estimates show the region accounts for 3.6 million people who developed TB in 2025 — 34% of the global total — and 4,00,000 TB-related deaths, or 35% of the global total. "These numbers are a stark reminder that TB remains one of the Region’s most pressing public health and development challenges,” said Nilesh Buddha, officer-in-charge, WHO South-East Asia Region.

A release issued by the regional office added that in 2025, $1.03 billion was available for TB prevention and care in the region, with 91% from domestic sources. Yet this represented only around 16% of global TB funding, despite the region accounting for 34% of global cases. "Closing this gap in resources is critical to sustaining progress," the WHO said.

“Ending TB is not simply a health sector responsibility. It requires leadership across government, sustained investment, strong health systems and communities at the centre of the response. We have tools to prevent, diagnose and treat TB. What is needed now is the commitment to ensure they reach everyone who needs them, without delay or financial hardship,” said Dr. Buddha, adding that ending TB by 2030 will depend on countries turning political commitments into measurable action, with greater urgency and scale.

Meanwhile, the Global TB Report said that across the world, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (more than 20% of total household income). This is far from the target of the WHO End TB Strategy of zero.

articles.title: Aaditya Thackeray calls for Climate Change Councils at Centre, State levels to tackle pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: At the State level, he proposed similar councils chaired by the respective Chief Ministers, with participation from relevant departments to monitor the implementation of climate action plans

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and former Maharashtra Environment Minister Aaditya Thackeray has called for the establishment of Climate Change Councils at the Central and State levels, modelled on the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, to ensure coordinated action against pollution and climate change.

In a post on X on Thursday, November 12, Mr. Thackeray criticised the Centre over deteriorating environmental conditions across the country and accused it of presenting misleading statistics and engaging in “greenwashing” rather than addressing the crisis.

He proposed that a central Climate Change Council be chaired by the Prime Minister and include Environment Ministers from all States. The council, he suggested, should meet every three months to review environmental data, climate targets and the progress made towards achieving them.

Referring to the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Türkiye and upcoming environmental events in Mumbai, including the Earthshot Prize and Mumbai Climate Week, Mr. Thackeray questioned the Centre’s commitment to fulfilling its international climate obligations.
He alleged that discrepancies between official environmental statistics and actual conditions had affected India’s standing on international climate indices.

Highlighting the impact of pollution on citizens, Mr. Thackeray said people were increasingly being forced to spend their own money on air purifiers, water purifiers and access to safe food despite paying direct and indirect taxes.

He also claimed that worsening environmental conditions were forcing some citizens to relocate and prompting businesses to consider leaving the country, potentially affecting employment opportunities.
Mr. Thackeray questioned whether the government was adequately addressing citizens’ basic needs, including access to clean air, safe drinking water and uncontaminated food.

articles.title: Trump administration will fund new research on controversial psychedelic drug ibogaine
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Federal officials say there’s new funding to study the medical potential of a powerful psychedelic

Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said his department is awarding up to $4.9 million to prepare for the first U.S. studies of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder, a hard-to-treat condition linked to higher suicide and substance abuse rates among veterans.
The money will not go directly to patient research, Kennedy said, but to lay the groundwork needed to manufacture, dose and design studies of the drug.

Ibogaine is made from a shrub native to West Africa. It can cause intense hallucinations, nausea, vomiting, tremors and sometimes deadly irregular heart rhythms. Ibogaine is currently illegal, in the same ultra-restrictive class as LSD, ecstasy and most other psychedelic drugs.

Veterans organisations and psychedelic advocates contend that ibogaine has great promise for intractable conditions such as PTSD, severe depression and opioid addiction. U.S. research on the drug has essentially been frozen for decades due to ibogaine's restricted status.

Kennedy said the government will receive data and treatment guidance from Beond Inc., a Texas-based company that has treated more than 3,000 patients with ibogaine in Mexico, where the drug is not illegal.
“That is going to allow us to dramatically accelerate the clinical trial process,” Kennedy said. “We’re going to have, I think, a record drug approval process.”
Additional funding awards may explore ibogaine's use for addiction, he said.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, who joined Kennedy for the announcement, said the collaborative effort would focus first on safety and “best-in-class research.”
“For veterans living with PTSD, we owe them both urgency and the best science we can produce,” Collins said.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre asks officials to blacklist Larsen & Toubro for ‘delaying’ works
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects.

The direction came after the final notice issued to the company that is executing drinking water facilities to 388 rural habitations in Dharwad district, Kalghatgi town, and eight en route rural habitations of Saundatti taluk, Belagavi district from the Renukasagar reservoir (Navilutheertha dam).

Sources said that though the work was awarded on April 20, 2022, to be completed by October 19, 2024, the progress on site was very slow. The daily pipeline progress is also less than 500 m per day, sources said.

It is learnt that instruction had been issued to complete trial run of all 126 villages, which are not affected by the proposals submitted by the Forest Department, to be completed within December, 2026, and the company was instructed to submit detailed week-wise completion plan for pipe procurement, laying, hydro testing and trial run.

Sources said that the officials informed the Minister during a meeting that despite the instructions, pipes allegedly had not been purchased, adequate number of workers had not been deployed and work was progressing slow, and that progress report was not being submitted.

In response, the Minister asked officials to black list L& T and issue final notice to all contractors who were delaying implementation of work, especially at a time when the State was reeling under drought.

articles.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the Keralam Police.

Calling for a comprehensive investigation, he urged the government to uncover the entire network behind the racket, fix accountability for the alleged intelligence lapses, strengthen inter-State police coordination and take stringent action against all those involved.

articles.title: Swachh Survekshan: Guntur wins ‘Super Swachh League’ award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Guntur finishes third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings
Guntur has won the ‘Super Swachh League’ award after finishing third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings.

Guntur Municipal Corporation Commissioner K. Mayur Ashok received the award from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi on Wednesday, along with Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar and APTIDCO Managing Director B. Sunil Kumar Reddy.
Andhra Pradesh has secured six national awards, emerging as the second-best performing State in the country.

Mr. Ashok attributed the achievement to the collective efforts of municipal officials, sanitation workers and public participation. He said several initiatives had been implemented to improve sanitation and scientific waste management in the city.

A waste-to-energy plant is operational, while a Letter of Award has been issued for establishing a new Bio-CBG plant to generate green energy from waste. The civic body has also introduced electric autos, compactors and modern sweeping machines to strengthen garbage collection, he said.
Scientific removal of legacy waste, the ‘Swarnandhra-Swachh Andhra’ programme and the 30-day ‘Operation Clean Sweep’ drive contributed to improving urban cleanliness, he said.
The Municipal Commissioner pledged to continue efforts to transform Guntur into a cleaner and better-maintained city.

articles.title: Recent repairs on OMR come undone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sholinganallur junction has a bad stretch of road that is riddled with potholes; portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart

Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that make driving on these roads difficult. These are the sections where the Chennai Metro Rail works are under way.
V. Raman, a resident of Mettukuppam, said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.

“I drive a van at times and many commuters like me have to slowdown at this spot. This leads to considerable slow down of traffic flow. It is worse during school hours with more vehicles on road. Service lanes are in a bad shape,” he said. The Sholinganallur junction has a particularly bad patch that is riddled with potholes. Repairs undertaken recently seem to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.

“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road. At times, the stones hit vehicles. Pedestrians find it very difficult to walk due to damages along the road,” he said.
Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart.
“The height of the road was unnecessarily increased. No study on rainwater flow was done before the re-laying, which is why it has led to flooding. We need an independent flood-risk study.”

The Sholinganallur junction has a bad stretch of road that is riddled with potholes; portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart

Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that make driving on these roads difficult. These are the sections where the Chennai Metro Rail works are under way.

V. Raman, a resident of Mettukuppam, said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.

“I drive a van at times and many commuters like me have to slowdown at this spot. This leads to considerable slow down of traffic flow. It is worse during school hours with more vehicles on road. Service lanes are in a bad shape,” he said. The Sholinganallur junction has a particularly bad patch that is riddled with potholes. Repairs undertaken recently seem to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.

“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road. At times, the stones hit vehicles. Pedestrians find it very difficult to walk due to damages along the road,” he said.

Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart.

“The height of the road was unnecessarily increased. No study on rainwater flow was done before the re-laying, which is why it has led to flooding. We need an independent flood-risk study.”

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: VS Hospitals introduces digital mammography system for breast cancer detection
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The system uses a 50-micron detector to capture detailed images of breast tissue, helping radiologists examine tiny microcalcifications that may be associated with early breast abnormalities
VS Hospitals has introduced a new 2D digital mammography system to strengthen breast cancer screening and diagnosis.

The AMULET SOPHINITY system from Fujifilm uses a high-resolution detector with a pixel size of 50 microns, allowing detailed imaging of breast tissue, including tiny microcalcifications, which can sometimes be an early indicator of breast abnormalities.

Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to examine breast tissue and can help identify abnormalities that may not be detectable through physical examination. The new system has intelligent exposure control, which adjusts X-ray exposure according to breast composition while maintaining image quality. AI-based positioning support is designed to assist in accurate positioning and consistent image acquisition.

The equipment takes approximately five seconds for standard image acquisition and 12 seconds for high-resolution imaging. It also has features such as flexible positioning, intelligent breast compression and automatic decompression to help reduce discomfort during the examination.

Speaking at the launch, S. Subramanian, Chairman and Managing Director of V.S. Hospitals, said early detection was important in breast cancer care and that mammography played a key role in identifying breast abnormalities.
The hospital will offer free mammography screening to underprivileged people throughout November 2026. Those seeking to avail themselves of the screening can contact the hospital at 7448850500.

articles.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Keralam government of concentrating decision-making powers in the hands of the Chief Minister, alleging that even ministers are being kept in the dark about important decisions.
He said the situation was unprecedented in the State and called for a judicial investigation into what he described as suspicious administrative actions.

Speaking at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] political explanation meeting at Chathurakkinar in Madikkai, Mr. Vijayan questioned how a Minister, who is also the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, could remain unaware of major decisions concerning his own department. He said governance was being conducted without proper coordination between departments, with the Chief Minister taking decisions independently.

Referring to the electricity purchase agreement with GNA, Mr. Vijayan said the Minister concerned had earlier said that he was unaware of the decision to enter into the agreement. The Minister was reportedly unaware even when the decision to abandon the agreement was taken, he said.
He also alleged that attempts were being made to create an artificial power shortage to benefit corporate monopolies.

articles.title: Kerala High Court orders government to ready adequate medicines, vehicles at mental health centres by November 24
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Stating that assurances alone are not sufficient, and they have to translate into action, the Kerala High Court has directed the government to make available adequate medicines and vehicles in mental health centres by November 24.

A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji, who had earlier this year visited the centres in Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur, and Kozhikode acceded to the Advocate General’s request to file an action taken report by the same day on the construction of compound walls and the appointment of necessary personnel at the centres.

This was after the Advocate General submitted that the construction of compound walls around the centres was progressing at a good speed. On the appointment of personnel, he sought another two weeks’ time, saying that there had been a change of incumbent in the post of Secretary, Health and Family Welfare department, and that he was in the process of evaluating the files concerned. The matter has been listed for hearing on November 24.

The High Court had in September expressed satisfaction at the government’s decision to rename mental health centres as “happiness and wellness centres”, observing that the (hitherto) stigmatisation of patients, their caregivers, and the centres as a whole was something one could not be oblivious to. The Advocate General had informed the court then that the government was looking into infrastructure and staff vacancy issues at the centres with ‘full sincerity’.

articles.title: Daughter of Cheranalloor accident victim files review petition before Kerala High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of Jayabalakrishnan who died after a luxury car reportedly driven by the minor son of a judicial officer rammed his two-wheeler at Cheranalloor here on October 25, has filed a criminal review petition before the Kerala High Court, challenging an order passed on November 5 by the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge (Children’s Court) granting bail to the minor in conflict with law (CCL).

In her petition, she submitted that the impugned judgment of the children’s court is ex facie illegal, perverse, and vitiated by a complete non-application of mind to the mandatory statutory exceptions embedded in the proviso to S.12(1) of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.

The court erred in holding that the gravity of the offence and the loss of human life cannot be factored into the assessment under the Section, whose proviso explicitly mandates the denial of bail, if release is likely to ‘defeat the ends of justice’ or ‘expose the child to moral, physical or psychological danger’. In high-fatality culpable homicide cases under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita committed through gross vehicular recklessness, releasing the CCL severely undermines public confidence in the rule of law and directly defeats the ends of justice, she said in her plea.

Political & National Report: Daughter of Cheranalloor accident victim files review petition before Kerala High Court. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Cochin shipyard, SFO Technologies jointly develop sophisticated laser arc welding technology

fullParagraphs: Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) and the Kochi-based SFO Technologies Private Limited have unveiled what is claimed to be the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured hybrid laser arc welding (HLAW) technology.

The announcement was made at the inauguration of the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and HLAW R&D facility at NeST Hitek Park, Kalamassery. The facility was inaugurated by Jose V.J., chairman and managing director, CSL, and N. Jehangir, chairman and managing director, SFO Technologies.

Jointly developed by CSL and SFO Technologies, the HLAW system integrates laser welding, conventional arc welding, robotics, and advanced automation, powered by a high-power fibre laser source indigenously developed by SFO Technologies, claimed a communication.

The technology is expected to deliver faster welding speeds, deeper penetration, lower distortion, and improved weld consistency across shipbuilding, defence, heavy engineering, railways, energy, and other strategic manufacturing sectors like large tanks and wagons for improving productivity, claimed the developers in a statement.

Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) and the Kochi-based SFO Technologies Private Limited have unveiled what is claimed to be the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured hybrid laser arc welding (HLAW) technology.

articles.title: Consultations with Governor ongoing to arrive at agreement over V-C appointment: Higher Education Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Even as the issue of Vice-Chancellor appointment is caught up in litigation, the government is in constant touch with the Governor to iron out the differences and find a common ground, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan said on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters at a National Education and Urdu Day Celebration organised by the Tamil Nadu Urdu Academy at the University of Madras, Mr. Viswanathan said that besides him, the School Education Minister and the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker also have met the Governor and held talks about appointment of Vice-Chancellors to the State-run universities.

“Just last week, School Education Minister Rajmohan, the Honourable Speaker and I met the Governor. Consultations are going on and some agreements are being reached. We will be able to speak openly once things finalise. We will be meeting him again in a week’s time,” he maintained.

As a stop-gap arrangement, senior professors have been appointed as Vice-Chancellors in-charge in Alagappa, Annamalai, and Manonmaniam Sundaranar Universities. “The Chancellor, the Chief Minister, and the Pro-Chancellor” all want a solution to the problem soon, he added.

Commenting on the first six months of the current government, he said that his Department had taken steps to solve issues pending for a long time, like extending the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) to teachers of government-aided colleges. “They had protested at least 52 times over the past five years,” he pointed out.
The government had also increased the honorarium of guest lecturers by ₹5,000 and has announced the implementation of free laptop scheme for college students at a cost of ₹2,000 crore.

He gave away awards and prizes to 23 teachers working in Urdu medium schools for 30 years, 10 Urdu poets and authors, and 627 students from 19 colleges and 39 schools who won various competitions like essay writing, elocution, and poetry. The Minister also assured the gathering that he would take their demand of a teachers’ training centre for Urdu teachers to the Chief Minister.

Present on the occasion were K. Navas Kani, MP and Chairman, Tamil Nadu Waqf Board, K.A.M. Muhammed Abubacker, former MLA and State General Secretary of IUML, Rita John, Registrar, UoM, and S. Armstrong, Member, Vice-Chancellor Convener Committee.

articles.title: Offering food, best dharma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R. Narayanan in a discourse. There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar. In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings. More importantly, we must always use sweet words. Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others.

Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam. Maranar was wealthy. He honoured devotees of Siva by washing their feet with scented water. He then offered them a lavish meal, which did not lack any flavour. The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty. He made sure that Maranar lost his wealth. Eventually, he was left with nothing but a tiled house and a small plot of land. One night, after Maranar had sown seeds in his field, it rained heavily. That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep. Maranar’s wife asked her husband to fetch the grains that had been sown that morning. She cleaned the grains, and used it to cook rice for the visitor. Usually, the grains used for sowing were never used for cooking, because they ensured that a farmer would be able to grow his next crop. So, something that would take care of a farmer’s future would never be used for food. But Maranar and his wife broke that rule, when they cooked for the mendicant. Greens grown in the backyard were also used to prepare tasty dishes. Since there was no firewood, Maranar’s wife used a wooden beam from their house as firewood. When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva. He blessed them and said they would reach Sivaloka.

articles.title: Haryana Congress to launch campaign to protect people’s voting rights, says Sanjay Dutt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: All India Congress Committee Haryana in-charge Sanjay Dutt and Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh will lead the two-week tour, participating in ‘Chaupals’ (community gatherings)

Haryana Congress will launch ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from November 12 to November 24 in the State, for what it terms an initiative to defend democracy, protect people’s voting rights and expose alleged electoral manipulation.

All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge of Haryana Sanjay Dutt and Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh will lead the two-week tour, participating in ‘Chaupals’ (community gatherings) across Haryana.
Mr. Dutt said the objective is to engage with people and mobilise public opinion in defence of democratic institutions and electoral integrity.

“The campaign assumes particular significance in Haryana, where the Congress party has raised serious questions about the integrity of the 2024 Assembly elections. Congress maintains that the people’s mandate in favour of the party was subverted through a systematic conspiracy of electoral manipulation,” he said in a statement.

“Our campaign will be much more than a series of public meetings. It is an initiative to take the fight for democracy directly to the people. Through these ‘Chaupals’, the Congress will expose electoral irregularities, sensitise citizens about the dangers of manipulated electoral rolls and build a statewide movement to safeguard every citizen’s fundamental democratic right to vote. We continue to reiterate the demand for the resignation and criminal investigation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The objective is unequivocal: every vote must be protected, every voter must be respected, and the Election Commission must function independently, impartially and without political interference,” he added.

Besides senior party leaders and functionaries, district Congress committee presidents, presidents and office-bearers of various frontal organisations, cells and departments from across Haryana will participate in this statewide campaign.

articles.title: Woman found dead at locked flat in Baranagar; police suspect sexual assault
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, the flat is owned by the victim’s sister and brother-in-law who had been staying there for the last four years. However, they had recently moved to Hooghly for their work
A 26-year-old woman was found dead at a flat in Kolkata’s Baranagar area on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with the police suspecting she was sexually assaulted before the murder.
According to the police, the flat is owned by the victim’s sister and brother-in-law, who had been staying there for the last four years. However, they had recently moved to Hooghly for their work.

“Two days ago, her brother-in-law handed over the key to a lady. But the victim took the key from her on Tuesday and went to the flat at the fifth floor of the apartment,” said a police official from Baranagar Police Station.
Later, her sister was trying to reach out to her over the phone. But she did not respond to her repeated calls prompting her sister to inform the matter to the local police station.

Upon receiving the information, the police arrived at the apartment late on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) night and broke open the door to recover her body. “She was lying dead on the floor. There were also multiple injuries visible on her body. It could be sexual assault before the murder. However, the fact will be ascertained once we get the autopsy report. Further probe is underway,” said the officer.

Reacting to the development, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress alleged that the local BJP leaders are trying to downplay the gravity of the incident. “These are the very people who came to power promising women safety, chanting Bhorsha in, Bhoy out. Today, under their watch, Bengal has become a land of fear for women, where not a shred of trust remains in the administration. Failed CM. Failed investigations. Zero accountability,” it said in a statement on X.
The party also said that random encounters and case closures are no substitute for justice. “Where is the thorough investigation? Where is the accountability? Where is the deterrence?” it asked.

articles.title: Punjab polls: Congress begins campaign; BJP takes a dig
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the State Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa launched the campaign at the party headquarters in Chandigarh

Even as the Congress party on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) began its public outreach campaign — ‘Punjab Mangda Insaaf’ (Punjab Demands Justice) — in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly election, the Bharatiya Janata Party hit out at the Congress over its campaign, saying that a party, whose leaders were involved in anti Sikhs riots in 1984 has no moral right to speak about “justice” in Punjab.

Leader of Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa and Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Pargat Singh participated in a series of engagements in Mohali as a part of the party’s campaign, which the party asserts to aim to build a collective movement against the growing menace of drugs, crime, corruption and the deteriorating law and order situation in Punjab.

Mr. Bajwa said the campaign was not merely a political campaign but a struggle for Punjab’s rights, dignity and a better future. “The Congress would bring together every section connected with Punjab, demand answers from the Aam Aadmi Party government and present a development roadmap for 2027 based on suggestions received from the people,” he said.

Punjab BJP President Kewal Singh Dhillon, meanwhile alleged that the claims made in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s newly released memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, concerning former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and the June 1984 Operation Blue Star, were calculated political ploy to whitewash the sins of the Congress.
“What does an ‘Insaaf Yatra’ mean in Punjab without full justice for the 1984 victims and a public, unconditional apology from Congress for its heinous crimes?” he said in a statement.

Mr. Dhillon alleged that for decades, successive Congress governments protected the guilty of anti-Sikh riots and handed out clean chits. “It was only after the Modi led BJP government took office in 2014 and constituted a dedicated Special Investigation Team (SIT) that justice finally caught up with the perpetrators,” he added.

articles.title: Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979”

U.S. President Donald Trump defended the war against Iran on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) at a U.S. Veterans Day commemoration that saw his Defence Secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum.
"The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible," Mr. Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington.
"When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer."

The war, which began on February 28 with U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 U.S. service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures.

Mr. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which "has been waging war on America since 1979." He stressed that U.S. forces were acting in order to halt Iran's capacity to build a nuclear weapon.
Mr. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America's lost service members.
During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Mr. Trump namechecked Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had "done a fantastic job."

Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) blocked an effort — launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker — to impeach Mr. Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Mr. Hegseth stirred even more controversy at the ceremony: an Army sentinel watching over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded a small group of people that included Mr. Hegseth, his wife and several aides, when some of them laughed after posing for a picture in front of the sacred site.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the sentinel called out, halting his patrol to face the group as they walked up some stairs to leave. Mr. Hegseth turned around to look at the guard.

articles.title: Rights panel steps in to address alleged contamination of well water near temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The PCB and temple committee have assured that water contamination near the temple will be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant becomes operational

A solution appears to be in sight to the alleged contamination of well water near the Thiruvarinikkulam Devi Temple during the 10-day-long Nadathurappu festival, attended by thousands each year, thanks to the intervention of State Human Rights Commission Chairperson Alexander Thomas.

The State Pollution Control Board (PCB) and the temple committee office-bearers assured the Commission that the issue of water contamination would be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant at the temple becomes operational.

The Commission directed the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat secretary to submit a report after testing a sample of well water from the temple’s neighbourhood once the treatment plant becomes operational. The directive was issued on a petition filed by Sujikumar, a resident living around 300 metres from the temple entrance, alleging that the water in his well became polluted during the temple festival.
The Kochi Sub-Collector submitted a report to the Commission, informing that the Kochi Devaswom Board, PCB, and the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat had been instructed to take emergency measures.

The report stated that a wastewater storage tank with a capacity of 6 lakh litres had been constructed. The PCB has directed the temple to use the treated water for agricultural purposes. The PCB and temple committee have assured that water contamination near the temple will be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant becomes operational

A solution appears to be in sight to the alleged contamination of well water near the Thiruvarinikkulam Devi Temple during the 10-day-long Nadathurappu festival, attended by thousands each year, thanks to the intervention of State Human Rights Commission Chairperson Alexander Thomas.

The State Pollution Control Board (PCB) and the temple committee office-bearers assured the Commission that the issue of water contamination would be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant at the temple becomes operational.

The Commission directed the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat secretary to submit a report after testing a sample of well water from the temple’s neighbourhood once the treatment plant becomes operational. The directive was issued on a petition filed by Sujikumar, a resident living around 300 metres from the temple entrance, alleging that the water in his well became polluted during the temple festival.

The Kochi Sub-Collector submitted a report to the Commission, informing that the Kochi Devaswom Board, PCB, and the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat had been instructed to take emergency measures.

The report stated that a wastewater storage tank with a capacity of 6 lakh litres had been constructed. The PCB has directed the temple to use the treated water for agricultural purposes. It also said that the new plant would be permitted to operate only in compliance with the Board’s guidelines. The 2026 festival will serve as a full-scale test to assess the plant’s efficiency.

The case will be heard next during the Commission’s sitting in September. The petitioner, the environmental engineer, and the panchayat secretary have been asked to appear.

articles.title: Two SPOs go missing in J&K's Kishtwar; massive search operation launched
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The officials said the two SPOs were travelling from Kiyar camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah when they failed to reach their destination

Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) went missing from the higher reaches of Dachhan in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Wednesday (November 12, 2026), prompting security forces to launch a massive joint search operation to trace them, officials said.

The missing personnel have been identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), both of whom were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at their Kiyar village in Dachhan, the officials said.

They said the two SPOs were travelling from Kiyar camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah when they failed to reach their destination. Their mobile phones were initially reachable but were later switched off, raising concerns about their whereabouts.
Following their disappearance, a massive search operation was launched jointly by the police and the Army's Rashtriya Rifles to locate the missing personnel.

Security teams were deployed in the surrounding areas, including difficult and mountainous forest terrain, to establish their whereabouts and ascertain the circumstances surrounding their disappearance, the officials said.
They said it would be premature to link the incident to any militant activity until the facts emerge.
However, the disappearance has drawn attention to the security situation in the mountainous district, which has witnessed a series of terror-related incidents over the past several years.

Kishtwar has remained a focus of security operations to eliminate the remaining militant presence in its remote and forested areas. Successive counter-insurgency operations have resulted in the killing of several active terrorists, significantly weakening their presence in the district.
Nevertheless, the difficult terrain and vast forested stretches continue to pose operational challenges for security agencies, the officials said.
The district has witnessed casualties among both security personnel and terrorists in recent years.

articles.title: Thousands struggling without water after a major leak in a pipeline in Kolkata’s Tala area
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, over 5 million gallons of water have been gushed out after the 72-inch pipeline got damaged on Monday (November 9, 2026) morning

Thousands of residents at Kolkata’s Tala area have been struggling without water for the last three days after a major water supply pipeline under the Tala bridge leaked. The incident also triggered severe waterlogging and impacted the train services in the city.

According to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, over 5 million gallons of water have been gushed out after the 72-inch pipeline got damaged on Monday (November 9, 2026) morning. The line ran also under the railway track due to which the tracks also got waterlogged, disrupting train services.
Water supply to neighbourhoods of Central Avenue, Rajabazar, College Street, Bidhan Sarani, Park Circus, AJC Bose Road, parts of Ballygunge got disrupted, said the KMC officials.

KMC also started the repair work but said that it may take two to three days to restore the entire system. The Tala reservoir can restore up to 44 million gallons of water and supply potable water to five booster pumping stations.

The Sealdah Division of railways is also closely monitoring the situation and is working towards restoring the services. “I am pleased to inform passengers that, from tomorrow onwards, all Mail/Express and suburban train services will operate on their normal routes. Sealdah Division has also made alternative arrangements to prevent water from entering the railway tracks and has developed an additional drainage system to minimise the possibility of such waterlogging in the future,” said DRM Rajeev Saxena.

Taking immediate cognisance of the incident, General Manager, Eastern Railway, Gitika Pandey, held discussions at the highest level of State Government of West Bengal and initiated immediate action by constituting a dedicated team to tackle the situation. Understanding the difficulties faced by passengers, particularly those travelling from Kolkata Station to reach their destinations for Chhath Puja, Sealdah Division made special arrangements for their comfort and convenience. Food packets, drinking water and other refreshments were distributed among passengers waiting for delayed trains to ensure that they did not face additional hardship during this difficult situation.

Due to waterlogging and its impact on the signalling system, Circular Railway passenger services remained regulated on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Railway officials and technical teams worked continuously to restore the affected systems and bring train operations back to normal.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, are facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.

articles.title: UN peacekeepers failed to protect civilians before South Sudan massacre: Amnesty
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director

United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to take adequate action despite warnings weeks before insurgents raided a village and killed more than 200 people earlier this year, Amnesty International said in a report released on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The rights group said that the peacekeeping mission, known by the acronym UNMISS, knew that an attack on Abiemnom, a remote area near the border with Sudan, was likely but failed to reinforce the roughly three dozen peacekeepers based there until after it occurred.
Between 1,000 and 1,500 armed men from neighbouring Mayom County carried out the March 1 attack, shooting residents, burning homes and looting part of the hospital, Amnesty said.
The death toll was at least 213, according to authorities, including 130 town residents, 76 security personnel and seven foreign nationals.

“Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director.

UNMISS spokesperson Priyanka Chowdhury said in a statement that the mission did its best with limited resources to provide protection and medical care to roughly 2,500 people who sheltered at a protected area established in anticipation of the attack.

Facing budget cuts and reduced personnel, she said that the mission "concentrated its available capacity on immediate protection of civilians seeking refuge within our base rather than dispersing limited forces across tasks they could not safely sustain simultaneously.”

The March assault came amid renewed fighting between government forces and an array of opposition groups, undermining a 2018 agreement that ended five years of civil war. The area has experienced cycles of retaliatory violence linked to land access and cattle raiding.
Amnesty said that the March attack may have been triggered by unresolved killings of several young men from neighbouring Mayom County in Abiemnom.
The investigation drew on interviews with 82 people, including survivors, witnesses and medical workers, along with satellite imagery and verified photographs and videos.

articles.title: NTR Health University scrutinises 1,622 applications for UG research programme
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: NTRUHS to earmark 10 to 25 grants from a pool of 200 Faculty Research Grants for PG students undertaking research projects independently of their mandatory dissertations

The Ph.D. and Research Committee of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS) has scrutinised 1,622 applications received under the Undergraduate Student Research Scholarships (UGSRS) 2026 programme during its three-day meeting held between November 9 and 11.
Apart from examining all 1,622 scholarship applications, the committee reviewed the six-month progress reports of Faculty Research Grant projects and Ph.D. scholars.
The meeting was held under the leadership of Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar. Registrar T. Sai Sudheer, Director (Research and Development) M. Lakshmi Surya Prabha, and others took part.

During the meeting, the committee decided to earmark 10 to 25 grants from a pool of 200 Faculty Research Grants for postgraduate students undertaking research projects independently of their mandatory dissertations.

According to a release by the university, the initiative aims to encourage postgraduate students to pursue additional research, develop scientific inquiry skills and gain experience in research design, data collection, analysis and scientific reporting. It is expected to provide opportunities for students to undertake research activities beyond their regular academic requirements.

The committee discussed the introduction of courses in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Health for undergraduate and postgraduate students. A separate meeting has been scheduled for November 19 to deliberate on the proposed courses.

The Ph.D. and Research Committee of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS) has scrutinised 1,622 applications received under the Undergraduate Student Research Scholarships (UGSRS) 2026 programme during its three-day meeting held between November 9 and 11.
