fullParagraphs: Around 300 passengers were travelling in the four affected coaches, railway officials said

Four AC coaches of the Gorakhpur-bound Chauri Chaura Express derailed shortly after the train left Kanpur Central railway station on Wednesday evening (November 11, 2026). No casualties were reported in the incident, senior police and railway officials said.
Around 300 passengers were travelling in the four affected coaches, they said.

"Chauri Chaura train [15003] bound for Gorakhpur from Anwar Ganj departed from platform number 7 at around 5.03 p.m.. As it moved out of the station, coaches B-4, B-5, B-6 and B-7 derailed, triggering panic among passengers," Commissioner of Police Raghubir Lal told PTI .

It was the second derailment incident reported in Wednesday (November 11, 2026). Earlier in the day, five coaches and the engine of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at Digaru near Assam's Guwahati, leaving four persons injured.
Railway officials and engineering teams rushed Kanpur to oversee restoration work. Senior railway officials from Prayagraj were also sent to Kanpur.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (East) Satyajeet Gupta said the derailment occurred at around 5.07 p.m. No passenger was injured, and the railway safety team would investigate the cause, he said.
All were safe and had been shifted to platform number 1, where arrangements for refreshments and a special train were being made for their onward journey, Mr. Gupta said.
The special train could take four to five hours to be arranged, a railway official said, adding that passengers unwilling to continue their journey would receive a full refund.
The incident did not affect other train operations at the station, the officials said.

A passenger travelling with his family for Chhath Puja said a sudden jolt threw his child to the floor. Panic-stricken people rushed out of the coaches before realising that four coaches had derailed.

articles.title: Environmental, social costs of Vizhinjam port railway tunnel to be higher than anticipated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposed tunnel between Balaramapuram and Vizhinjam to provide rail connectivity to Vizhinjam International Seaport has triggered serious environmental and land stability concerns in the region

The State government’s decision to construct a railway tunnel to Vizhinjam International Seaport costing over ₹1,500 crore through a densely populated region, despite the availability of an alternative land alignment, has raised eyebrows among many, with experts and members of the public questioning its environmental and social costs against the backdrop of the State government’s stated commitment to sustainable development.

The proposed tunnel between Balaramapuram and Vizhinjam to provide rail connectivity to Vizhinjam International Seaport has triggered serious environmental and land stability concerns in the region. The project, which is set to become the State’s second major tunnel project and the country’s third-longest railway tunnel, has been disputed by experts regarding its feasibility beneath the Vizhinjam-Balaramapuram road, who termed it potentially unviable given the region’s fragile geology, soil types and high population density.

Dr. V. Nandakumar, former head of the Natural Hazards Research Group and former director (In charge) of the National Centre for Earth Science Studies, said no comprehensive study involving competent national institutions appeared to have been conducted on the geological formations along the proposed 10.7-km alignment, variations in soil types or the east-to-west groundwater flow before the project was taken up.

Drawing on more than three decades of field experience, Mr. Nandakumar said most stretches of the proposed alignment are likely to pass through geologically weak terrain. Beneath the top layer of laterite, the subsurface is expected to comprise of decomposed lithomargic clay interspersed with hard rock in some locations. Other sections consist of inconsistent red soil underlain by layers of clay and sand. Such formations, according to him, are unsuitable for a tunnel carrying container trains weighing several tonnes.

The proposed alignment also passes through some of the most densely populated areas of Thiruvananthapuram district, where a large section of the population depends on open wells for drinking water. He warned that the impervious concrete tunnel structure, laid at a depth of around 30 metres, could act as an underground barrier, disrupting the natural movement of groundwater. This could eventually cause wells to dry up in an area already facing water scarcity.

He also flagged the risk of vibrations generated by heavy container trains passing through tunnels bored into weak soil. Such vibrations could damage existing structures, ranging from large buildings to smaller houses, causing cracks and, in extreme cases, structural collapse. Land subsidence and building damage could pose long-term risks along the entire stretch, he cautioned.

He also opined whether authorities had adequately explored an alternative alignment through lower-lying areas, including the fringes of the Pallichal-Mudavoorpara paddy fields, which is elevation-wise 10 m lower than the proposed tunnel alignment, which is 30 m below the road surface and almost having a parallel elevation with the port and the Trivandrum- Nagercoil rail link. Such a route, according to him, could avoid potential hazards to densely populated areas and minimise risks to existing structures, groundwater resources, environmental stability and local livelihoods.

It could also reduce construction and maintenance costs. A surface-level alignment would also offer greater scope for future track doubling and expansion, which would be difficult to achieve with the proposed tunnel, he said. The project in its present form could destabilise the region and may disrupt the livelihoods of millions of people living along the Balaramapuram-Vizhinjam corridor. The land above the tunnel, including the buffer zone, could remain locked subject to restrictions on development, building permits and other uses. This also may even affect property ownership and transfer rights. The disposal of excavated rock and soil generated during tunnelling could pose another major environmental challenge.

He urged the government to reconsider the tunnel proposal and instead opt for an overland railway alignment after establishing its economic viability. Senior government officials said they selected the alignment as the shortest route from the existing railway lines to the port, although an overland alignment with relatively lower cost is available through a paddy field in the region.

articles.title: First phase of Musi rejuvenation to begin shortly, says Telangana CM Revath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister said the lake would become a new destination alongside Shilparamam and called for developing a lake economy around it

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Wednesday said the first phase of the Musi rejuvenation project would begin shortly, asserting that the river had to be cleaned up and restored rather than merely beautified. He said the government would ensure that no one suffers losses in the process and called for the cooperation of all political parties.

Speaking at the inauguration of the revived Thammidikunta Lake, he said Musi river pollution was causing hardships to people in Nalgonda district, who were paying the price for the neglect of successive governments. The lives of Hyderabad residents were closely linked to the river, he said.

Recalling the construction of Osmansagar and Himayatsagar reservoirs by the Nizam to protect Hyderabad from floods, he said the Musi riverfront had been developed nearly a century ago, but the water body had now become polluted.

Describing Hyderabad as a city of rocks and lakes, Mr. Revanth Reddy said it had 1,372 lakes, but nearly 50% had disappeared due to various reasons. Encroachments had resulted in waterlogging on roads and flooding of residential colonies during rains. He stressed the need to free lakes from encroachments as part of efforts to protect nature and establish Hyderabad as a global city.

He said Thammidikunta Lake had been expanded from 14 to 30 acres, keeping the future of coming generations in mind, even if some people suffered losses in the process. Actor Akkineni Nagarjuna had voluntarily handed over two acres of land to the government, he said, describing him as a hero in real life as well as in films.

The Chief Minister said the lake would become a new destination alongside Shilparamam and called for developing a lake economy around it. He directed police officials to ensure adequate security and suggested planting a Jammi tree on the lake premises so that lakes could become venues for Dasara celebrations and help preserve cultural traditions.

articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race
Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang 's has global implications.

The 63-year-old is the leading face of the artificial intelligence revolution with his black leather jacket and fluff of grey hair. He runs the company Nvidia, which produces highly coveted computer chips. That's landed him on a late-night phone call with President Donald Trump , a promoter of the industry.

But Mr. Huang was also liaising with a Chinese businesswoman who has allegedly fed intelligence — as well as advanced chips — to China. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed.

It's a saga of personal betrayal, corporate espionage and high-tech development, and the fallout is spreading across Washington. There are bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill. The U.S. Department of Justice has opened its own probe. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, is conducting an internal review.

Some expect the technology to reshape human civilisation by imbuing computers with the vast powers of creation and analysis, and Mr. Trump has repeated that “whoever wins AI, wins." Nvidia is the backbone of America's plans for dominating the field.
When asked about Mr. Huang's affair, Mr. Trump said this week that he had spoken to the tech executive as the scandal grew.
“I think he'll be in good shape," President Trump said, adding that "he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
As for when the President first learned about the concerns involving Ms. Alice Huang, Mr. Trump brushed off the question.
“They could have been mentioned," he said. "Certainly it didn't make much of an impact on me.”
With the AI race between the U.S. and China often framed as a fierce and consequential rivalry , the Justice Department has persistently warned of the espionage threat posed by Beijing.

articles.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Moutaz Eyad Daghlas was killed in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, late on Monday (November 9, 2026), the Palestinian health ministry said.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds and took them to hospital, but that Israeli forces blocked access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
The Israeli military, asked by AFP about the incident, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) it had acted to "thwart stone-hurling and terrorist attacks" in the area.

"The soldiers identified several terrorists who intended to hurl stones at a highway used by Israeli vehicles. This was in an area where stones have recently been hurled at Israeli vehicles," the military said.
"The soldiers responded by firing towards them in order to remove the threat."
Israeli forces have routinely opened live fire on Palestinians including minors who throw stones in the West Bank, which Israel has controlled since 1967.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said Israeli forces killed at least 241 children or teenagers in the territory between the October 7, 2023 attack by Gaza-based Hamas and late June this year.

Violence has increased in recent weeks, especially in the run-up to Israel's October 27 election, before which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to appeal to hardline settlers in the West Bank.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.

articles.title: Indian billionaire, doctors spar over $900 brain blood-flow tracker Temple
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Promotional materials for the device, developed by Deepinder Goyal, ‌say that its BrainFlow feature shows how well the brain is being supplied with blood in real time

A tiny, $900 wearable device being developed by an Indian billionaire entrepreneur and showcased by some ‌of the country’s top sportspersons has sparked criticism from doctors who say its claims ​of tracking blood flow to the brain are exaggerated.
The Temple device is less ⁠than 1 inch (2.54 cm) wide and weighs under 2 grams (0.07 oz). It sticks to the side of the head between the forehead and the ear, or the temple area.

Promotional materials for the device, developed by Deepinder Goyal, ‌say that its BrainFlow feature shows how well the brain is being supplied with blood in real time and its Entropy feature can detect how hard the ‌body works to shed heat.
It can also measure thermal, immune, digestive, cognitive and emotional readings ‌that ⁠help to transform how a person regulates their health, they say.
Priced at 85,000 ⁠rupees ($907), the device comes in six colours. India’s cricket captain Shubman Gill and Olympic medal-winning badminton player P.V. Sindhu have worn it.

Some well-known doctors in the country, however, are sceptical of the claims, saying the device’s capabilities are not backed by ​peer-reviewed research. In prime-time shows and on social ‌media, they are calling for the device to come under the purview of medical regulators.
Prominent Indian hepatologist Cyriac Philips, known as “TheLiverDoc”, has been criticising the device on his X account with 328,000 followers, calling Temple “the biggest health scam”.
“People must be aware of wellness hacks such as ‌wearables also, even though they are not marketed as health devices,” he told Reuters.
On one ​prime-time TV discussion, paediatrician and nephrologist Sanjeev Bagai called Temple a “gimmick”, saying it had “no formal approval or clearance”.
Goyal has hit back at the criticism from doctors, ⁠saying Temple is a “fitness tracker, and wellness device”, not a medical one.

articles.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: One ​of the world’s biggest ‌smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales

Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a “performance-focused ​reduction” following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told ‌staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, ​with notifications set to begin in November.
The ⁠cuts are part of an effort to build “a stronger performance culture” and address situations where the company “has consistently fallen short of ‌expectations,” Amon said.
The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could ‌not immediately determine the scale of the cuts.

Qualcomm ‌did ⁠not immediately respond to a request for comment. ⁠It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September.
One ​of the world’s biggest ‌smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets.
Its shares have ‌risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of ​more than 12% for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor ⁠Index.
Qualcomm shares were up more than 1% after trading down about 0.5% earlier on Tuesday.

In its latest earnings report ‌in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-centre and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027.
The company expects the majority of its chip sales ‌to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as ​it expands into the fast-growing AI data-centre market.
Amon said in the memo business priorities, organisational needs, skills ⁠and expertise would be considered in making the cuts.

One ​of the world’s biggest ‌smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales

Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a “performance-focused ​reduction” following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told ‌staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, ​with notifications set to begin in November.

The ⁠cuts are part of an effort to build “a stronger performance culture” and address situations where the company “has consistently fallen short of ‌expectations,” Amon said.

The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could ‌not immediately determine the scale of the cuts.

Qualcomm ‌did ⁠not immediately respond to a request for comment. ⁠It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September.

One ​of the world’s biggest ‌smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets.

Its shares have ‌risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of ​more than 12% for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor ⁠Index.

Qualcomm shares were up more than 1% after trading down about 0.5% earlier on Tuesday.

In its latest earnings report ‌in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-centre and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027.

The company expects the majority of its chip sales ‌to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as ​it expands into the fast-growing AI data-centre market.

Amon said in the memo business priorities, organisational needs, skills ⁠and expertise would be considered in making the cuts.

Ms. Gandhi played a pivotal role in the political decision-making that ultimately led to the formation of Telangana. Her contribution to the Statehood process has been widely acknowledged in Telangana, particularly in view of the historic struggle and the aspirations of its people.

articles.title: Keralam CM hails Muslim brothers for performing Hindu woman’s last rites
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘This is the Keralam I know, love and believe in,’ Satheesan said in a post on X, sharing the story of Razak and Sulaiman

Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) hailed two Muslim brothers who performed the last rites of an 85-year-old Hindu woman they had cared for as their mother for nearly five decades in Wayanad district.
“This is the Keralam I know, love and believe in,” Mr. Satheesan said in a post on X, sharing the story of Razak and Sulaiman, whose touching gesture was reported by the media a day earlier.

The two brothers performed the funeral rituals of Kalyani Amma, who had no children or other relatives, in accordance with Hindu customs after she passed away at Chithragiri in Muppainad panchayat, family sources said.

Razak and Sulaiman, along with their family, had shared a close bond with Kalyani Amma, who had been their neighbour for nearly 50 years. They looked after her daily needs, arranged medicines and accompanied her to hospitals whenever necessary.
She was also part of their family celebrations, and the affection between them grew over the years.
Kalyani Amma had expressed her wish that the two brothers, whom she considered her own sons, should perform her last rites after her death.
Respecting her wish, they lit her funeral pyre and performed the final rites at a local Hindu crematorium.
In his post, Satheesan said the brothers had “fulfilled the woman’s final wish with the love and dignity of her own sons”.
“A mother’s love does not check religion. A son’s duty does not ask about caste. And grief, like love, belongs to all of us equally,” he said.

Describing the incident as a heartwarming example of Keralam’s spirit, the Chief Minister said the State was a land where “love knows no religion, compassion knows no caste, and humanity brings us together”.

articles.title: Gorakhpur-bound Chauri Chaura Express derails in Kanpur: A look at other recent train accidents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kolkata-Sairang Express incident has brought renewed attention to rail safety and the safeguards in place to avoid a major mishap.
Gorakhpur-bound Chauri Chaura Express derailed on November 11, 2026, shortly after leaving Kanpur Central railway station, in Uttar Pradesh.
Four coaches of the train derailed. No casualties were reported in the incident, senior police and railway officials said, according to a report published in The Hindu.

On the same day, the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at the Digaru railway station in Assam, with several coaches going off track after the loco pilot failed to control the train’s speed while giving precedence to another train. The Northeast Frontier Railway said that all passengers are safe and no injuries have been reported.
The incidents have brought renewed attention to rail safety and the safeguards in place to avoid a major mishap.

In July 2026, the Ministry of Railways issued a press release in which it detailed that the country had witnessed ‘only two consequential train accidents until that month.’ A consequential train accident refers to an accident which resulted in the loss of human lives/injury or damage to railway property or interruption to rail traffic in excess of laid-down threshold levels.

The Safety Information Management System (SIMS ) of the Indian Railways, in its ‘recent train accidents’ section , lists the accidents that occurred from April 1 2025, to present. The November 11, 2026, Kolkata-Sairang Express derailment has not been added to the database till the date of publication.
Here are the consequential train accidents of the recent past

On November 6, 2026, at 1.00 p.m., a fire broke out in the Karmabhoomi Express near Sarai Banjara railway station in Punjab’s Patiala district. Eyewitnesses and residents who rushed to the spot said thick smoke could be seen billowing into the sky as the coaches caught fire, according to a report in The Hindu.
Senior railway officials said the fire initially broke out in one coach but spread to other coaches due to strong winds. No casualty or injuries were reported.

On July 17, 2026, at 6:41 a.m., the Nimtita-Katwa passenger train dashed into a Tata Sumo four-wheeler between Khagraghat Road and Karnasubarna stations of the Howrah Division. No casualties or property damage was reported.

articles.title: Amish Shah, Pia Dandiya join centrist New Democratic Coalition
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The other prominent caucus within the Democratic party – the progressives – has over 100 members and is led by Texas Congressman Greg Casar with lawmakers Ilhan Omar, Pramila Jayapal and Ro Khanna as members

Newly elected Indian-American U.S. lawmakers Amish Shah and Pia Dandiya have joined the New Democrat Coalition, which now has 142 members, making the centrist group the largest ideological bloc within the party.
The New Democrat Coalition, led by Brad Schneider, inducted 40 new members-elect into the group on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the single largest addition in its 30-year history.

“When I first came to Congress in 2012, the New Dems had 43 Members. Fourteen years later, New Dems are proud to welcome 40 new members, our largest freshman class ever, and now number 142 Members,” Mr. Schneider said in a statement.

The other prominent caucus within the Democratic party – the progressives – has over 100 members and is led by Texas Congressman Greg Casar with lawmakers Ilhan Omar, Pramila Jayapal and Ro Khanna as members.
Besides Mr. Shah and Ms. Dandiya, the New Democrat Coalition has Ami Bera, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar and Raja Krishnamoorthi as members.
Mr. Thanedar and Mr. Krishnamoorthi are not part of the new House of Representatives that will take office on January 3 as they lost the Democratic primary for the House and Senate respectively.
Mr. Shah, an emergency medicine doctor and three-term member of the Arizona House, traces his familial roots to Gujarat.

Born in Chicago, Mr. Shah’s parents immigrated to the U.S. in the 1960s. He earned his undergraduate degree at Northwestern University and his medical degree at Northwestern University Medical School as part of the Honours Program in Medical Education. His father is Jain and his mother is Hindu.

He received a full merit scholarship to obtain a Master’s in Public Health at the University of California, Berkeley, followed by residency training in Emergency Medicine at New York City's busiest Level-1 trauma center.

Ms. Dandiya is a first-generation American who has dedicated her career to strengthening communities as a high school principal, policy leader and technology innovator, according to her campaign website.

articles.title: U.S. Defence Secretary Hegseth, staff reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be heard, and the soldier guarding the tomb shouted that “all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times”

A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery.

Video shows Mr. Hegseth taking photos on the empty steps in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.
As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be heard, and the soldier guarding the tomb shouted that “all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.”
Sean Parnell, the Pentagon's top spokesman, said that “while commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.”
“The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured — and will always honour — the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe,” he added.

The tomb is considered to be one of the most solemn and revered war memorials in the U.S., being the final resting place of unidentified soldiers from World War I, World War II and the Korean War. It has been guarded around the clock — rain or shine — by a soldier from the Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, also known as “The Old Guard," since 1948.
Mr. Hegseth and his staff were at the tomb as part of a larger ceremony commemorating Veterans Day that was also attended by President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance.
The incident comes a day after Mr. Hegseth narrowly survived an effort to impeach him by lawmakers in Congress.

articles.title: Protesters clash with police in Spain after huge housing cost rallies
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez

Police fired tear gas as sporadic clashes broke out in Madrid and Barcelona on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after huge protests across Spain over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election.

Hundreds of thousands of protesters turned out during Spain's first nationwide 24-hour strike since 2012, with authorities estimating around 120,000 demonstrators marched through the capital and more than 50,000 rallied in Barcelona.
Clashes broke out after the protests in Spain's two largest cities, as groups of hooded and masked demonstrators hurled projectiles at police and sparked fires, according to AFP journalists.
Video footage showed large rubbish skips as well as bicycles and pot plants engulfed in flames on roads in Barcelona with heavy contingents of police vans racing through the streets.
Police used rubber bullet launchers and tear gas to disperse small groups of protesters and arrested 18 people in Barcelona.

The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
Braving pouring rain, protesters in Madrid carried placards shaped like houses and chanted "we have no home" as they called for more affordable housing.
"People work a lot and it isn't enough to pay the rent, to pay for a house," Paula Diaz, a 25-year-old theatre technician who lives with her parents, told AFP at the Madrid protest.
"I hope a government that benefits us comes to power, especially the working class," she added, referring to the November 29 election.

In Barcelona, where authorities estimated 55,000 people marched through the city's luxury Passeig de Gracia commercial thoroughfare, Maria Pinana told AFP "the law of supply and demand does not apply to housing".

fullParagraphs: Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access

An elite North Korean hacking group’s $6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to ‌compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold ​into a massive theft.

The October 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in ⁠a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance’s initial investigation.

Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee’s computer or ‌credentials are compromised.

Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global’s OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider. The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards ‌and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer’s computer — like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and ‌moving ⁠assets.

Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, Alexander said, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates ⁠to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain’s decentralized ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.

“I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be ​unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that ‌need to avoid censorship,” Alexander said. “In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that.”

The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, ‌transaction controls and other defenses.

“I do expect we’ll see more clarity and standardization in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements ​for investor protection and trust,” Alexander said. “These things show why it has to change.”

That has made engineers and IT workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.

articles.title: Illegal oocyte collection racket: 27 ART centres inspected across Telangana, notices issued to seven hospitals
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities

The Telangana Health Department has intensified its investigation into the alleged illegal oocyte (egg) collection racket, with inspections conducted at 27 of the 44 identified Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) facilities across the State. Officials have detected 13 regulatory violations in seven hospitals and issued show-cause notices to their managements.

Health Minister C. Damodar Rajanarasimha has directed the department to conduct a comprehensive investigation into alleged illegal activities being carried out under the guise of oocyte collection and initiate stringent action against institutions and individuals found violating prescribed regulations.
Acting on the Minister’s directions, task force teams have been inspecting IVF centres across the State for the past four days. Inspections at the remaining facilities are continuing.

The department said further action would be initiated after a detailed examination of records seized by the police and information obtained from the National ART and Surrogacy Registry. The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities.

As part of the investigation, the Health department officials visited the National ART and Surrogacy Registry in New Delhi on November 6 and sought details of the data submitted by registered ART clinics and ART banks operating in Telangana.

The department has reiterated that oocyte collection must strictly comply with the provisions of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act and Rules. All ART clinics and ART banks operating in the State are required to obtain mandatory statutory registration and adhere to the prescribed regulatory framework.

The Health Department also cautioned women against falling prey to misleading assurances and financial inducements offered by intermediaries, warning that such arrangements could expose them to unauthorised medical procedures.

articles.title: Keralam to launch Family Sustainability Mapping to identify children in high-risk environments
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna says circumstances of families and children will be assessed with cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and police

The Keralam government will take steps to implement ‘Family Sustainability Mapping’ across the State to identify, at an early stage, children living in high-risk environments, Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna has said.

Speaking at a press conference to announce the Ujjwala Balyam Awards on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), she said a decision regarding the mapping was reached during a meeting convened following the death of a two-year-old child in Alappuzha recently due to suspected malnutrition.

The circumstances of families and children will be assessed with the cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and the police. Children facing risks such as malnutrition, neglect, domestic abuse, child labour, begging, school dropouts, substance abuse-related issues or various forms of exploitation will be identified and necessary protection and rehabilitation will be ensured.

“Child protection efforts should not be limited to intervening only after abuse or exploitation has already occurred. The government’s objective is to proactively identify high risk situations and ensure timely protection for children. Coordinated action among various departments and institutions will be strengthened to prevent issues such as sexual abuse, physical and mental abuse, neglect, child labour, child begging, human trafficking and online exploitation,” she said.

Activities will be jointly coordinated by departments including the Department of Women and Child Development, the Health Department, the Police, and the Local Self Government Department. Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna says circumstances of families and children will be assessed with cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and police

The Keralam government will take steps to implement ‘Family Sustainability Mapping’ across the State to identify, at an early stage, children living in high-risk environments, Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna has said.

Speaking at a press conference to announce the Ujjwala Balyam Awards on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), she said a decision regarding the mapping was reached during a meeting convened following the death of a two-year-old child in Alappuzha recently due to suspected malnutrition.

The circumstances of families and children will be assessed with the cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and the police. Children facing risks such as malnutrition, neglect, domestic abuse, child labour, begging, school dropouts, substance abuse-related issues or various forms of exploitation will be identified and necessary protection and rehabilitation will be ensured.

“Child protection efforts should not be limited to intervening only after abuse or exploitation has already occurred. The government’s objective is to proactively identify high risk situations and ensure timely protection for children. Coordinated action among various departments and institutions will be strengthened to prevent issues such as sexual abuse, physical and mental abuse, neglect, child labour, child begging, human trafficking and online exploitation,” she said.

Activities will be jointly coordinated by departments including the Department of Women and Child Development, the Health Department, the Police, and the Local Self Government Department. This will enable the strengthening of existing child protection systems as well as the proactive identification of risks and the implementation of preventive measures. The Minister stated that the active participation of society is essential to ensure a safe childhood and equal opportunities for every child and to create an environment in which they can grow up with self confidence.

articles.title: Military-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist, records show
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls on China’s access to advanced AI chips, such as chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports

A Chinese university with deep ‌ties to the People’s Liberation Army bought Nvidia’s powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, ​highlighting gaps in Washington’s efforts to curb China’s access to advanced technology.

The findings come as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting scrutiny in ⁠Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on sales of AI chips to China, following reports alleging he was targeted by a Chinese spying operation.

Huang has argued that continued US sales to China would preserve American technological leadership and keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology. But some US lawmakers say access to Nvidia’s most powerful AI chips can speed China’s development of AI systems for weapons design, ‌intelligence analysis and military modernisation.

Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls on China’s access to advanced AI chips, such as chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports. Three Republican congressional committee chairmen have requested a briefing with Huang on November 18 over his reported contacts with an alleged Chinese ‌intelligence operative.
Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website.
Northwestern is a member of the “Seven Sons ‌of ⁠National Defense” group of Chinese universities under U.S. sanctions and with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing.
The chips were purchased for its management ⁠school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows.

The H200 is among Nvidia’s most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems and is subject to US export licence approvals, which are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical.

Northwestern Polytechnical also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies, procurement records show.

Reuters is ​reporting the chip purchases and computing contracts for the first time. Northwestern ‌Polytechnical, Nvidia and the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export controls, did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not determine contact details for Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology.

articles.title: Temperatures drop further in Telangana; lowest of 11.3°C in Sangareddy

fullParagraphs: The minimum temperatures in Telangana 33 districts were less than 15.2°C

Temperatures continue to fall in Telangana as the lowest of 11.3°C was recorded in Sangareddy between the mornings (8.30 a.m.) on Wednesday and Thursday (November 12, 2026). The minimum temperatures in the 33 districts were less than 15.2°C.

The lowest of 11.3°C in Sangareddy was followed by 11.4°C in Rangareddy; 11.7°C in Vikarabad; 12.0°C in Mahabubnagar; 12.2°C in Kumaram Bheem Asifabad; 12.4°C in Nagarkurnool; 12.7°C in Siddipet and Kamareddy; 12.8°C in Rajanna Sircilla and 13.1°C in Medak, according to Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report.

Besides Rangareddy, the two other urban districts in the State too recorded colder temperatures. While the minimum temperature in Medchal Malkajgiri was 13.2°C, it was 15.1°C in Hyderabad. The temperatures have been low from the past a few days.

India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Thursday has forecast minimum temperatures likely to be below normal by 2°C to 3°C during the next two days. Maximum and minimum temperatures in Hyderabad and neighbourhoods are likely to be around 32°C and 17°C respectively over the next 48 hours, according to its forecast on Thursday afternoon.

articles.title: LPST rankholders resume stir in front of Keralam Secretariat after police remove protesters on hunger strike
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dramatic scenes unfold as LPST Rankholders’ Association secretary Valarmathi returns to resume her fast-unto-death protest. Stir reached a flashpoint on Wednesday night when Cantonment police forcibly removed Valarmathi and dismantled protesters’ shed and flex boards

Dramatic scenes unfolded in front of the Secretariat on Thursday noon, where the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association is on the 130th day of its agitation, with S. Valarmathi, the association secretary, returning to resume her fast-unto-death protest after being forcibly removed from the protest site by the police on Wednesday night citing her deteriorating health.
The protest reached a flashpoint on Wednesday night when the Cantonment police forcibly removed Ms. Valarmathi and dismantled the protesters’ shed and flex boards.
LPST rankholders at the protest site in front of the Secretariat on Thursday | Photo Credit: Nirmal Harindran

Ms. Valarmathi, who was on the 16th day of her fast-unto-death when the police shifted her to the General Hospital, told reporters on Thursday that she would not give up until the government met their demands. If the government was concerned about her health, it should take the initiative to resolve the strike, she said.
M. Jayakrishnan, another rankholder who launched a hunger strike in Ms. Valarmathi’s place on Wednesday night, will also continue his fast-unto-death.

The police action late on Wednesday night triggered widespread protests, with Yuva Morcha and DYFI workers, along with CPI(M) leaders P.K. Biju and C.S. Sujatha, reaching the spot. DYFI leaders then swiftly moved in to put up replacement sheds after the police had removed the original ones.

The police maintained that they had served a notice to the protesters earlier in the day regarding the removal of the shed and flex boards. They also said they had removed only the permanent shed put up by the protesters at the site where the fast was being held.

The strike appeared to have gained considerable political traction following the police action on Wednesday night, with the Opposition closing ranks on Thursday and extending its support to the protesters while condemning the government’s attempts to “put down” the agitation.

Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, speaking to reporters on Thursday morning, said the government had no animosity towards the protesters and that the police had been forced to remove the protesters’ shed to avoid contempt of court proceedings, following the Supreme Court’s recent decision against the indefinite occupation of public roads and spaces for protests and its directive that authorities clear obstructions to public ways.
He added that the police were facing constant flak from courts over non-compliance with court directives on issues such as this.

articles.title: Owaisi names Chandrashekhar Azad as Uttar Pradesh CM face of Samajik Parivartan Morcha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a joint press conference with the AIMIM chief, Mr. Azad said, “If SP, Congress or any other party wants to join us to stop BJP from coming to power, we are open to it”

Asaduddin Owaisi’s All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and Chandrashekhar Azad’s Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) announced the formation of a new alliance, the ‘Samajik Parivartan Morcha’, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, at a joint press conference in Lucknow on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
“We have decided to form S amajik Parivartan Morcha. I can say with confidence that this will be a strong Morcha to stop the BJP from coming to power in UP for the third time,” Mr. Owaisi said.
“If SP, Congress or any other party wants to join us to stop BJP from coming to power, we are open to it,” said the Nagina MP Mr. Azad.
Mr. Owaisi announced that Mr. Azad will be SPM coalition’s Chief Ministerial face for the 2027 State election.
“I am happy to announce that our brother Chandrashekhar Azad will be the chief president of the SPM and its chief ministerial candidate in Uttar Pradesh,” Mr. Owaisi said.

The AIMIM chief said the alliance would focus on issues concerning backward and Dalit communities, the oppressed and marginalised sections, irrespective of their caste, alleging that these communities had so far been used merely as vote banks by political parties.
He said the morcha would raise issues such as the deteriorating condition of education, unemployment among the State’s youth and problems faced by farmers.

The alliance between the two parties could pave the way for a first declared non-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), non-Congress political front in Uttar Pradesh, with both parties considered marginal players eyeing to consolidate Scheduled Caste (SC) and minority voters in the politically crucial state.

“The alliance will be aiming to focus on Dalit and minority voters, as both leaders have long been associated with these vote blocks, but getting votes or winning your own seat and making your candidates victorious is a different issue,” said Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, adding that the State is increasingly transforming into bipolar politics, between NDA and INDIA bloc, and it would be a huge challenge for the new alliance to make an impact.

articles.title: Pawan Kalyan pitches Andhra Pradesh as trusted global hub; Lokesh unveils red-carpet framework at 31st Vizag CII Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Lokesh urged corporate leaders to move beyond setting up manufacturing units and relocate their primary corporate headquarters to Andhra Pradesh, citing superior quality of life, skilled talent pipelines, and seamless connectivity anchored by new ports and the Bhogapuram International Airport

Projecting Andhra Pradesh as a dynamic gateway for global capital, Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and IT and Industries Minister Nara Lokesh rolled out an aggressive growth agenda at the inaugural session of the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on Thursday (November 12, 2026), pitching the State as a secure, fast-paced corporate destination.

Setting the tone, Mr. Pawan Kalyan positioned the State as a reliable, investor-friendly hub backed by robust political stability and transparent governance. Commending Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s long-term vision and Mr. Lokesh’s aggressive industrial outreach, Mr. Pawan Kalyan urged global investors to leverage the State’s expansive coastal infrastructure and green energy potential.

Striking a personal chord before addressing the delegates, the Deputy Chief Minister joined traditional folk artistes in beating drums and interacted warmly with venue sanitation workers, drawing widespread applause.

Taking the dais, Mr. Lokesh unveiled an ambitious picture of industrial transformation, announcing that the government has attracted ₹22.6 lakh crore in investment commitments since June 2024, with 73% of these projects already receiving regulatory clearances. articles.title: Keralam ration dealers seek GPS tracking of lorries to prevent foodgrain diversion from NFSA godowns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demand comes against backdrop of Keralam govt’s decision to install CCTV cameras in ration shops and integrate e-PoS machines with weighing scales to ensure accuracy in distribution of ration commodities. Dealers point out that monitoring should extend to every stage of supply chain

Ration dealers in Keralam have demanded the installation of GPS tracking devices in lorries transporting foodgrains from National Food Security Act (NFSA) godowns to ration shops to prevent the diversion of essential commodities into the black market and ensure transparency in the public distribution system.

The demand comes against the backdrop of the State Government’s decision to install CCTV cameras in ration shops and integrate electronic Point of Sale (e-PoS) machines with weighing scales to ensure accuracy in the distribution of ration commodities. While welcoming the move, dealers have pointed out that monitoring should extend to every stage of the supply chain, particularly the transportation and storage of foodgrains.

They have called for GPS-enabled tracking of all lorries carrying ration commodities from godowns to retail outlets. The system would enable authorities to monitor vehicle movements, verify delivery routes and identify possible diversion of foodgrains before they reach the designated ration shops. It would also help establish accountability in the transportation of essential commodities.

The dealers have further demanded the installation of CCTV cameras at NFSA godowns to monitor the loading and dispatch of foodgrains. They said the weighing systems at godowns should also be linked with those at ration shops to ensure that the quantity dispatched matches the quantity received.

According to T. Mohammed Ali, State General Secretary of the All-Kerala Retail Ration Dealers Association, the e-PoS machines at ration shops should be connected to the weighing systems at NFSA godowns as well. This would help eliminate discrepancies in weight and ensure that beneficiaries receive their full entitlement.

The association has urged the government to hold discussions with dealer representatives and address the shortcomings in the existing distribution system. It maintains that installing CCTV cameras only at ration shops would not be sufficient to prevent irregularities unless the movement of commodities from godowns is also effectively monitored.

The dealers have also raised concerns over the financial viability of ration shops, citing rising operating expenses and declining income. Nearly eight ration shops have reportedly closed in the Kozhikode city limits over the past three years, while more than 500 shops are said to have shut down across the State.

The dealers have disputed the authorities’ claim that a ration shop generates around ₹30,000 in monthly income, arguing that the amount does not adequately cover expenses such as rent and electricity charges. They said it was high time the government prevented leakages, strengthen accountability and restore public confidence in the State’s ration distribution network.

articles.title: Sunita Williams serves as Grand Marshal at 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The parade brought together veterans, military families, service members, marching bands, community organisations, and supporters to “recognise the courage, service, and sacrifice of America's military heroes”
Indian-origin NASA astronaut Sunita ‘Suni’ Williams has served as the Grand Marshal for the 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade.

Ms. Williams, a U.S. Navy veteran, was joined by thousands of American veterans, active-duty military personnel, marching bands, patriotic organisations, military vehicles, and participants at the annual parade honouring those who served the country through the years.
Addressing the gathering, which included Indian-descent New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Ms. Williams said she is “humbly honoured” to be at the 107th New York Veterans Day Parade.

“When I joined the military, I never thought for a moment that I would actually be a veteran...thinking you're so young and how you're going to conduct your life. But my first steps in the military showed me the foundation with which I led my life: courage, honour, commitment,” she said.
Ms. Williams also highlighted the opportunity she had to work and live in space with people from all over the world.

“I can't thank the military enough for the time I have spent, the lessons I have learned, and looking forward to giving those lessons to the next generation and seeing how they can do even more than we've ever dreamed of,” she said, adding that “exploration is in our heart and in our soul.”

“Freedom is not free, and we have shown that time and time again by being role models for the world in our journey for exploration and for brotherhood and sisterhood throughout this planet,” she said.

Separately, in a statement, Ms. Williams said, “It is an incredible honour to serve as Grand Marshal of the NYC Veterans Day Parade and to march alongside my fellow veterans. My time in the Navy shaped who I am and prepared me for every challenge that followed. I'm proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honouring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation.”
Grand Marshal Sunita "Suni" L. Williams takes part in a Veterans Day parade on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, New York City. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Mark Otto, President and Executive Director of the United War Veterans Council and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, said: “We are incredibly proud to welcome Suni as Grand Marshal of this year's NYC Veterans Day Parade on the 250th birthday of the United States of America."

The parade brought together veterans, military families, service members, marching bands, community organisations, and supporters to “recognise the courage, service, and sacrifice of America's military heroes”

Indian-origin NASA astronaut Sunita ‘Suni’ Williams has served as the Grand Marshal for the 107th New York City Veterans Day Parade.

Ms. Williams, a U.S. Navy veteran, was joined by thousands of American veterans, active-duty military personnel, marching bands, patriotic organisations, military vehicles, and participants at the annual parade honouring those who served the country through the years.

Addressing the gathering, which included Indian-descent New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Ms. Williams said she is “humbly honoured” to be at the 107th New York Veterans Day Parade.

“When I joined the military, I never thought for a moment that I would actually be a veteran...thinking you're so young and how you're going to conduct your life. But my first steps in the military showed me the foundation with which I led my life: courage, honour, commitment,” she said.

Ms. Williams also highlighted the opportunity she had to work and live in space with people from all over the world.

“I can't thank the military enough for the time I have spent, the lessons I have learned, and looking forward to giving those lessons to the next generation and seeing how they can do even more than we've ever dreamed of,” she said, adding that “exploration is in our heart and in our soul.”

“Freedom is not free, and we have shown that time and time again by being role models for the world in our journey for exploration and for brotherhood and sisterhood throughout this planet,” she said.

Separately, in a statement, Ms. Williams said, “It is an incredible honour to serve as Grand Marshal of the NYC Veterans Day Parade and to march alongside my fellow veterans. My time in the Navy shaped who I am and prepared me for every challenge that followed. I'm proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honouring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation.”

Grand Marshal Sunita "Suni" L. Williams takes part in a Veterans Day parade on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, New York City. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Mark Otto, President and Executive Director of the United War Veterans Council and U.S. Marine Corps veteran, said: “We are incredibly proud to welcome Suni as Grand Marshal of this year's NYC Veterans Day Parade on the 250th birthday of the United States of America."

articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of the U.S.-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan "under a standard business visitor status" and there were "no special flags" about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers.

Mr. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan's Parliament in response to lawmakers' questions about Alice Huang's entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements.
"At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information," Mr. Chiu said.
"If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management."
Mr. Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said.

"If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review," Mr. Chiu said.
"For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country."

articles.title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of U.S. curbs
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, per sources

Chinese ‌artificial intelligence companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centres outside China, ​concerned that a scandal involving the U.S. chipmaker’s chief executive Jensen Huang could spur Washington to ⁠tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors, three people familiar with the matter said.

The moves underline concern among Chinese technology companies over the potential closing of a gap in U.S. export controls. Seeking to protect U.S. dominance of the ‌critical sector, Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence chips, but Chinese companies can access such processors remotely by renting computing power at data centres overseas.

A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, the people said. The people declined to be identified, or ⁠to identify the cloud provider because of the sensitivity of the matter.
Smaller AI labs are considering similar steps, including approaching major providers of rented computing power in Southeast Asia, two of the people said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces possible ouster amid fresh affair allegations

The companies fear the controversy surrounding Huang could add political momentum to ​the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, a ‌U.S. bill that would give the Commerce Department authority to regulate remote, cloud-based access to restricted technology, the people said. The House of Representatives passed the bill in January by a 369-22 vote, and it awaits Senate action.

Advanced Nvidia processors are used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots ‌and other generative AI products. Restricting overseas cloud access would make it harder for Chinese developers to ​obtain high-end computing power without importing the chips directly.

Huang said on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times reported that the woman involved ⁠was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed, and that U.S. authorities had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Reuters could not independently verify that allegation, which China has denied.

Alice Huang had business dealings and ‌investment ties with several leading Chinese technology companies, including Tencent and Alibaba, according to two people familiar with the matter. Tencent and Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation

Revelations that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen ​Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker’s board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for ‌the company and concerns about the board’s ability to investigate its CEO independently.

Among corporate leaders, “There have definitely been affair scandals and ​sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No,” said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.

Lipton was using a ⁠term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang’s relationship, a day after Nvidia’s board launched an internal investigation “regarding the national security concerns raised ‌in news reports,” according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.

The stakes are high. While it is not clear if Huang violated the company’s code of conduct or what penalties Huang could face, its bylaws allow his removal “with ‌or without cause” by the vote of a majority of directors.
The company’s advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI ‌superiority. ⁠China’s Foreign Ministry called the spying claim “a groundless accusation, slander and a smear.”
Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as ⁠close ties to Trump. Huang owns 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.
Shares in Nvidia were down 6% on Tuesday, extending their losses from Monday over fallout from Huang’s affair.

Unusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three ​independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark ‌Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.
The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple’s Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.

articles.title: Indoor air pollution poses critical, year-round health threat
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Outdoor emissions regularly infiltrate living spaces, combining with domestic activities to create complex, toxic indoor environments

As Delhi, and various other parts in the northern parts of India , brace for severe winter smog, spokespeople for consumer durable makers LG and Dyson said that the air inside homes, too, presents a critical, year-round health threat. Outdoor emissions regularly infiltrate living spaces, combining with domestic activities to create complex, toxic indoor environments.

Citing the 2026 Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) analysis, an LG spokesperson said that Delhi’s winter PM2.5 pollution stems from secondary particulates (27%), transport (23%), biomass burning (20%), dust (15%), and industry (9%).

Closing doors and windows does not make homes airtight as outdoor pollutants enter through micro-gaps. They then mix with emissions from cooking, incense, candles, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from paints and furniture, and human respiratory particles.

Alex Hudson, a Dyson engineer, said that indoor air pollution is rarely driven by a single origin as even walking on carpets and sitting on sofas can stir up settled dust particles into breathing zones.
The impact extends beyond respiratory irritation as the LG spokesperson highlighted the alarming cognitive toll on children’s brain development.

A 2021 study in World Development linked higher short-term air pollution exposure among Indian children aged 5–16 to significantly lower reading and mathematics scores. A 2022 working paper by the Institute of Economic Growth and IIT Delhi confirmed similar cognitive declines in children aged 8–11.

Furthermore, a 2024 analysis in Environmental Health involving 4,860 children across three continents found that every 1 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 0.27-point drop in full-scale IQ. For older adults, cumulative exposure accelerates cardiovascular disease, stroke, and COPD risks.
Dyson’s spokesperson told that young children breathe more air relative to their body size, making them particularly vulnerable given that people spend up to 90% of their time indoors.

To combat indoor pollution, Dyson recommends source control such as using low-VOC products, installing microfibre doormats, and deep cleaning carpets with HEPA-filter vacuums. LG suggested monitoring outdoor AQI via the CPCB’s SAMEER app or IQAir to schedule ventilation, alongside kitchen exhaust fans.

When choosing air purifiers, LG advises evaluating real-time sensing, comprehensive filtration (HEPA for particles and activated carbon for gases), and clean air delivery rate (CADR) for room-wide airflow. Addressing energy concerns, LG noted modern air purifiers consume roughly 1.73 units per day under continuous 24-hour operation, costing approximately ₹14 daily.

Alex Hudson, a Dyson engineer, said that indoor air pollution is rarely driven by a single origin as even walking on carpets and sitting on sofas can stir up settled dust particles into breathing zones.

The impact extends beyond respiratory irritation as the LG spokesperson highlighted the alarming cognitive toll on children’s brain development.

A 2021 study in World Development linked higher short-term air pollution exposure among Indian children aged 5–16 to significantly lower reading and mathematics scores. A 2022 working paper by the Institute of Economic Growth and IIT Delhi confirmed similar cognitive declines in children aged 8–11.

Furthermore, a 2024 analysis in Environmental Health involving 4,860 children across three continents found that every 1 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 0.27-point drop in full-scale IQ. For older adults, cumulative exposure accelerates cardiovascular disease, stroke, and COPD risks.

Dyson’s spokesperson told that young children breathe more air relative to their body size, making them particularly vulnerable given that people spend up to 90% of their time indoors.

To combat indoor pollution, Dyson recommends source control such as using low-VOC products, installing microfibre doormats, and deep cleaning carpets with HEPA-filter vacuums. LG suggested monitoring outdoor AQI via the CPCB’s SAMEER app or IQAir to schedule ventilation, alongside kitchen exhaust fans.

When choosing air purifiers, LG advises evaluating real-time sensing, comprehensive filtration (HEPA for particles and activated carbon for gases), and clean air delivery rate (CADR) for room-wide airflow. Addressing energy concerns, LG noted modern air purifiers consume roughly 1.73 units per day under continuous 24-hour operation, costing approximately ₹14 daily.

articles.title: Minor fire at Srikalahasti temple kitchen contained, no major damage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kitchen staff tried to bring the fire under control, but when it began to go beyond their ability to manage, the panicked workers rushed out of the building, thereby averting a mishap
A minor fire was reported in the kitchen attached to the famed Srikalahastheeswara Swamy temple in Srikalahasti town of Tirupati district on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The fire accident was attributed to an electrical short circuit, which aggravated when the ghee kept for making the “Prasadam,” meant to be offered to the deity before distribution to the public, caught fire from the stove and spread to the entire hall.
The kitchen staff tried to bring the fire under control, but when it began to go beyond their ability to manage, the panicked workers rushed out of the building, thereby averting a mishap.
After the temple staff initially tried to tame the flames with the fire safety equipment on hand, fire personnel stepped in promptly and brought the raging fire under control.
The queue line was closed, and devotees were barred from entering the temple premises until the fire was extinguished.
No major damage was reported from this incident, said the temple’s executive officer, B. K. Venkatesulu.

articles.title: Two lose nearly ₹1 crore in separate online trading frauds in Keralam’s Kozhikode
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Preliminary investigations revealed that the duped funds were systematically routed through multiple mule bank accounts and current accounts rented specifically for the operation by the accused

In two separate incidents of cyber fraud, a homemaker from Kodanchery and a farmer from Thiruvambadi, both in Kozhikode district of Keralam, lost ₹49.20 lakh and ₹49.10 lakh, respectively, after being lured into fake online trading schemes. The Cyber Crime Police and the Thiruvambadi Police have registered cases and launched a joint investigation.

According to the police, the person from Kodanchery fell prey to a fraudulent investment scheme after being persuaded by a morphed video featuring Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Facebook. The scammers convinced her that substantial financial returns could be generated through online trading.

In the second incident, the farmer, a former non-resident Indian (NRI), was allegedly defrauded through a fabricated video on YouTube. The perpetrators duped him into believing that importing medical equipment from abroad into India would yield high profits, prompting him to transfer funds to accounts specified by the scammers.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the defrauded money was systematically routed through multiple mule bank accounts and current accounts rented specifically for the operation by the accused.

Expressing concern over the rise of deepfakes and fabricated videos circulating on social media platforms, law enforcement agencies have urged the public to exercise caution when encountering lucrative online investment offers. The Cyber Police have also instructed bank officials to remain vigilant about unusual transactions and suspicious account activities.

The perpetrators duped him into believing that importing medical equipment from abroad into India would yield high profits, prompting him to transfer funds to accounts specified by the scammers.

Preliminary investigations revealed that the defrauded money was systematically routed through multiple mule bank accounts and current accounts rented specifically for the operation by the accused.

Expressing concern over the rise of deepfakes and fabricated videos circulating on social media platforms, law enforcement agencies have urged the public to exercise caution when encountering lucrative online investment offers. The Cyber Police have also instructed bank officials to remain vigilant about unusual transactions and suspicious account activities.
