articles.title: Kejriwal, his daughter get death threat from ‘Bishnoi gang member’; case filed in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh alleged caller demanded ₹7 crore from Mr. Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal if the money was not paid

The Punjab Police has registered a case following a complaint filed by Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, who claimed to have received a death threat message concerning party leader Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter, along with a demand for ₹7 crore.
The MLA lodged his complaint with the Mohali police, which registered a case under relevant sections of the BNS and the Information and Technology Act.

In his complaint to the Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police, Tilak Nagar MLA Singh claimed that he received both a call and a WhatsApp message on his mobile phone on November 6 from an individual, claiming to be a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
The alleged caller demanded ₹7 crore from Mr. Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal if the money was not paid, according to the complaint filed by the AAP MLA.

In his complaint, which is part of the FIR, Mr. Singh claimed that the caller stated, "Lawrence Bishnoi gang se bol raha hun, Arvind Kejriwal ko bol de, 7 crore de do nahin to Arvind Kejriwal or uski ladki Harshita Kejriwal ko jaan se maar dunga." (I am speaking from the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Tell Arvind Kejriwal that if he does not pay Rs 7 crore, then I will kill both him and his daughter.)
ALSO WATCH Tiger Shroff shooting: Is Lawrence Bishnoi the new Bollywood don? | Insight India

"Given his stature as a high-profile figure, the threat has caused national and public security risks. The sender has unlawfully used my position as an elected representative to channel extortionist demands and death threats directed at Arvind Kejriwal and his family. The acts committed by the sender constitute serious offences," Mr. Singh wrote in his complaint.

The Delhi MLA also requested a comprehensive investigation and to trace the CDRs, IP logs and location of the device to arrest the culprit before anything untoward happens. Necessary coordination with relevant law enforcement and security authorities should also be initiated to ensure full protection for the targeted individuals, he said.

Following the complaint, the Mohali police registered a case under relevant sections including 308 (4) (extortion), 351 (2) (criminal intimidation), 351 (4) (criminal intimidation by anonymous communication, 111 (2) (organised crime) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the relevant section of the IT Act at the Cyber Crime Police Station in Mohali.

articles.title: ‘Whiskers and Tails’ to be launched on November 13 in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Siri Soraba, the seven-year-old writer, has also illustrated her stories.
A book of six short stories by Siri Soraba, a Class II student at Kumaran’s, will be launched on November 13, the eve of Children’s Day, in Bengaluru.

Titled Whiskers and Tails , the book captures the lively and enchanting world of animals and a dash of magic. “Crafted in innocence and edged with loads of curiosity, the stories portray the positive spirit that the young author champions. The seven-year-old writer has also illustrated her stories,” said a release from the publishers.
The event will also have a session on the late Venugopala Soraba, English professor and writer in Kannada and English, who would have turned 90 this month. He is the grandfather of Siri.
The book will be launched at Wadia Hall, Indian Institute of World Culture, BP Wadia Road, Basavanagudi, between 10.30 a.m. and 1 p.m.

articles.title: Iran’s Guards say ‘accident’ left two tankers on fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that two tankers carrying over four million barrels of oil had caught fire after an "accident" on an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz.
Since the outbreak of the war in West Asia in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic shipping channel, insisting vessels use routes it has approved.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.

"Last night, two tankers - acting in violation of regulations and despite repeated warnings from the Revolutionary Guards Navy regarding the unauthorised and dangerous nature of the southern maritime route - were involved in an accident while traversing this prohibited path in the strait," the Guards said in a statement.
They did not specify the nature of the "accident" but said it left the two tankers immobilised after they were hit with a "violent explosion".

"These two supertankers were carrying a combined total of over four million barrels of oil, which are now ablaze - a consequence of the blind trust placed in the aggressive American military," the statement said.
Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
Tehran has often said they struck mines, but the U.S. military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

articles.title: OpenAI now allows enterprises to process AI requests within India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The facility initially supports GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI’s API, allowing requests to be processed and AI responses generated within the country to address enterprise data localisation requirements

OpenAI on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced local processing and inference for its API in India , allowing eligible businesses and developers to have supported AI requests processed and model computations performed within the country.

The move expands the company’s existing data residency offering in India, which was introduced in May 2025 and allowed eligible customers to store their data in the country. The latest development extends this capability to cover where the AI model processes information and generates responses, addressing a key concern among businesses handling sensitive information.

Initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model, the new offering is aimed at organisations that have not fully deployed artificial intelligence in business operations because of requirements around where their information is processed. This is particularly relevant to customers in financial services with specific data localisation requirements, OpenAI said.

“Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country,” said Nitin Bawankule, Head of Enterprise - India, OpenAI.

“Local inference gives them more control over where supported workloads run and helps address a practical barrier to adoption. It gives more businesses a way to put OpenAI’s tools to work, and gives Indian developers and startups more scope to build for their own, and enterprise needs.”

Under the new arrangement, both the processing of an API request and the model computation that generates its response will take place in India for supported workloads. Supported customer content will also be stored in the country, the company said.

The launch covers direct API usage and currently supports GPT-6 Luna input and output through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. Customers can access the capability by creating a new API project, selecting India for both storage and processing, and using the corresponding India regional endpoint.

The development comes as OpenAI expands its presence in India. Earlier this year, the company introduced OpenAI for India, an initiative spanning AI infrastructure, enterprise adoption, skills development and local partnerships. The initiative included a partnership with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data-centre capacity, according to OpenAI.

OpenAI models were also made available for in-country inference through Amazon Web Services’ Bedrock platform. AWS announced the availability of OpenAI models on Bedrock in August 2026, including regional inference capabilities for supported models.
OpenAI said its now launched API inference residency offering is available in other parts of the world, with India, Australia and Japan among the latest markets to receive the capability.

articles.title: Six researchers win Infosys Science Foundation prizes for 2026
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A total of 222 applications were received across six categories with the highest for ‘Engineering and Computer Science’ category, ISF said

The Infosys Science Foundation (ISF) on Thursday (November 12, 2026) announced the winners of the ‘Infosys Prize 2026’ in six categories — Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences.
Among the recipients is Riddhipratim Basu, Associate Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (ICTS-TIFR) in Bengaluru.

The prize for each category comprises a gold medal, a citation, and a prize purse of $100,000 (or its equivalent in Indian rupees). The laureates of Infosys Prize 2026 were selected by an international panel of jurors comprising renowned scholars and experts.

This year 222 applications were received compared to 150 last year, ISF Trustee Kris Gopalakrishnan said. He added that the highest number of applications were received in the Engineering and Computer Science category and the youngest winner this year is 31 years of age.

ISF said that from 2024, the prize has shifted focus to honour researchers under the age of 40, emphasising the need for early recognition of exceptional talent. “This encouragement of early career researchers will serve as an inspiration for the next generation of scholars and future innovators,” it said.

“Recognising exceptional researchers early in their careers is particularly important, as it gives them the encouragement and opportunity to pursue bold questions, challenge established thinking and make lasting contributions to their fields,” ISF President Srinath Batni said.
Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics and Public Affairs at Princeton University, has won the award for his contributions to the field of climate change, and technological innovation, and to the study of business cycle fluctuations. “His work provides deep insights into how societies adapt to climate change through technological innovations and is likely to have far-reaching policy implications,” the jury said.
Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Swarun Kumar, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, has been awarded in this category for his pioneering work that extends low-power wireless networks beyond information delivery to perception and action in the physical world. He combines insights on the physics of wireless technology with novel architectures and algorithms to obtain innovative designs in connectivity, sensing, control, and actuation.

articles.title: After being called a ‘Gujarati friend’, PM Modi extends festival greetings to Sam Pitroda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Overseas Congress chief said he and his wife met Mr. Modi in the past and the Prime Minister had been very warm towards them.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 12, 2026) conveyed Deepavali greetings to Sam Pitroda, a bitter critic of him and the BJP-led government, after the Indian Overseas Congress chief described him as a "Gujarati friend".
"Happy Diwali and Nutan Varsh Abhinandan to you Sam Bhai and to Anjana Ben. Praying for a joyful and healthy year ahead. Jai Jagannath," Modi said in a post on X.
Happy Diwali and Nutan Varsh Abhinandan to you Sam Bhai and to Anjana Ben. Praying for a joyful and healthy year ahead. Jai Jagannath! @sampitroda
Earlier, Mr. Pitroda, a close associate of Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, said that Modi is a “Gujarati friend” and he respects him as a person.
Mr. Pitroda said he and his wife met Modi in the past and the Prime Minister had been very warm towards them.

"I have nothing against Mr. Modi as a Gujarati leader, friend or well-wisher. He has been very warm towards me, and I appreciate that. Similarly, I have been to his house in Gujarat several times," Mr. Pitroda was quoted as saying by a news agency.
After Mr. Modi's response to Mr. Pitroda, an X user named Mihir Jha posted with a crying emoji, "Sam Pitroda ko Diwali wish kar saktey hain toh humein bhi wish kar do Modi Ji."
To this, Mr. Modi replied, "Aapko Bhi Happy Diwali Mihir Bhai. Have a great festive season and year ahead" and added a grinning emoji.

articles.title: Major reshuffle of IPS officers in Telangana | Mahesh Bhagwat is new Commissioner of Hyderabad Police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana government on Thursday (November 12, 2026) effected a major reshuffle of IPS officers, appointing Mahesh Muralidhar Bhagwat as the new Hyderabad Police Commissioner, replacing V.C. Sajjanar — who has been transferred as Director General of Telangana Fire, Disaster Response, Emergency and Civil Defence.

According to a Government Order issued by the General Administration Department, Soumya Mishra — who was serving as Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services — was transferred as DGP, Women and Safety, SHE Teams and Bharosa. She will also hold additional charge as DGP, Organisation and DGP (Legal).
IPS officer Soumya Mishra. File | Photo Credit: VENKATACHALAPATHY_C
Swati Lakra, who was serving as DGP, Organisation and Home Guards, has been appointed Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services. She will also hold additional charge as DGP, Home Guards.
IPS officer Swati Lakra (on the left) with former DGP Shivadhar Reddy and Mahesh Bhagwat (on the right). File

Charu Sinha has been appointed Director General of the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), while retaining additional charge as DGP, CID. She was previously holding additional responsibilities as DGP, Women and Safety, SHE Teams and Bharosa, and Director General of the ACB.
Anil Kumar, who was serving as DGP (Operations), Greyhounds and Octopus, has been transferred as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC).

Vikram Singh Mann has been appointed DGP (Operations), Greyhounds and Octopus, replacing Anil Kumar. He will also hold additional charge as DGP, Police Housing Corporation, and DGP, Special Protection Force.

Y. Nagi Reddy has been appointed Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Ex-officio Principal Secretary to the Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department. He will also hold additional charge as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Civil Supplies Corporation and Controller of Legal Metrology.
M. Stephen Raveendra has been posted as Director of the Telangana Traffic Management, Road and Rail Safety Bureau (TG-TMARS).

articles.title: At IAF commanders' meet, Rajnath calls for sharper surveillance, 'element of surprise'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday (November 12, 2026) urged the military to strengthen both the offensive and defensive aspects of the "element of surprise" to maintain combat readiness against conventional and emerging threats posed by the evolving nature of modern warfare.
In an address at the Air Force Commanders' Conference, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities and identify potential threats before they unfold.
The Defence Minister added that a rapidly shifting security environment demands continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness.

"Our defence forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy," he said.
Mr. Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh during an interaction at the IAF Commanders’ Conference, in New Delhi. Source: X/@rajnathsingh

"Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge," he added.
Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, the Defence Minister said drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare.
He exhorted the Air Force commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations.
The Minister called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space.

articles.title: Phage therapy holds promise in fighting against antimicrobial resistance: Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dr. Kalyan noted that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail

Phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to selectively eliminate harmful bacteria, holds significant potential in combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR), said Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy Koganti, sepsis and infectious diseases specialist at SHRI Hospital, Guntur.

He said this while sharing his research experience in a press release, after presenting his team's scientific findings at an international symposium jointly organised by the Chinese University of Hong Kong and reputed biomedical research journals.

Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy said his team's research presentation on phage therapy received appreciation from participants at the symposium. Dr. Sutharsan Govindarajan, Associate Professor and phage biologist, SRM University, AP, also presented research conducted by the team.

He described the event as an enriching learning experience, particularly the discussions on the wider applications of bacteriophages in diagnostics and therapy, including cancer research. Professor Chuanbin Mao, chair of the symposium, has been researching bacteriophages for 25 years and has contributed extensively to scientific literature, he said.
Dr. Kalyan noted that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail.

His team has administered phage therapy to a few patients at its centre with encouraging results. In collaboration with SRM University and Szeged University, Hungary, the team is working to advance its availability in India.

articles.title: Sanction granted by PMO to prosecute two IAS officers in Tamil Nadu, Madras High Court told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Anand Venkatesh directs DVAC to proceed with the process of filing charge sheet against former AIADMK Minister S.P. Velmunai and IAS officers K.S. Kandasamy and K. Vijaya Karthikeyan in the ₹98.25-crore corporation tender irregularities case

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) has accorded sanction to prosecute two IAS officers, K.S. Kandasamy and K. Vijaya Karthikeyan, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, in connection with the ₹98.25-crore corporation tender irregularities case, primarily registered against former AIADMK Minister S.P. Velumani, the Madras High Court was told on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Justice N. Anand Venkatesh recorded the submission made by Additional Solicitor General A.R.L. Sundaresan, assisted by Central government senior panel counsel V. Chandrasekar, and directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to proceed with the process of filing the charge sheet against all the accused in the corruption case pending for long.

Referring to the long-drawn process involved in obtaining sanction to prosecute the two IAS officers, ever since the complainant Jayaram Venkatesan of Arappor Iyakkam filed a contempt of court petition against the DVAC officials in 2025, the judge said: “It is a classic case of how much of effort had to be put in to obtain sanction to prosecute IAS officers in criminal cases.”

He also said: “The wheels (of law enforcement) move faster against poor people, but for influential people, the wheels hardly move.” The judge, last year, issued a series of directions to the State government to send the files to the Centre and then suo motu impleaded the Department of Personnel and Tranining (DoPT) in New Delhi in order to make it expedite the process of obtaining sanction.

After the ASG submitted a copy of the sanction order before the court on Thursday, the judge ordered the deletion of the DoPT from the array of respondents since it was not a necessary party in the contempt proceedings any more. He decided to keep the contempt petition pending only for the purpose of monitoring the further progress to be made by the DVAC.

In the contempt petition filed through its counsel V. Suresh, Arappor Iyakkam told the court that its complaint was related to irregularities in the award of Greater Chennai and Coimbatore municipal corporation civil contracts issued between 2014 and 2018 when Mr. Velumani served as the Minister for Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department during the AIADMK rule.

The DVAC registered a First Information Report (FIR), on the basis of the complaint, in 2021 and completed the probe a few years later. On February 12, 2024, then Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Speaker M. Appavu granted sanction to prosecute Mr. Velumani. However, as there was a delay in obtaining sanction to prosecute the two IAS officers, Arappor Iyakkam had filed the contempt petition last year.

Following continuous nudging by the High Court, the Tamil Nadu government forwarded its proposal for grant of sanction to the DoPT along with voluminous documents, which had to be translated from Tamil to English. Thereafer, on September 16, 2026, Sushil Kumar Patel, Joint Secretary, DoPT, told Justice Venkatesh that the PMO was the competent authority to grant sanction to prosecute IAS officers.

He said, the DoPT had sent the files to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) for its remarks and that it would forward the files to the PMO after receipt of the CVC’s remarks. Then, the officer had also assured the court that the entire process of obtaining sanction would be completed within two months.

articles.title: Venezuela tells COP31 it has sovereign right to pump more oil
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Venezuela’s Acting President ​Delcy Rodriguez’s comments at the UN ‌talks on Turkiye’s Mediterranean coast jar with efforts by other conference leaders to convince global governments to accelerate a ‌shift from carbon-emitting fossil fuels

Venezuela’s Acting President ​Delcy Rodriguez told the COP31 climate conference on Thursday (November 12, 2026) ⁠that the country has the sovereign right to develop its oil industry, even as it recognises the importance of combating climate change.
But they dovetail with the United ‌States' ⁠efforts to raise billions of dollars towards increasing oil output in ⁠Venezuela, a member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

"We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national ​development," Ms. Rodriguez told the summit. "It is ‌possible to grow and protect the environment at the same time."

Venezuela's forests acted as a "lung for the planet", absorbing more carbon than the country emits, she added. She did not address the impact ‌that oil exported from the country had on global emissions.

President ​Donald Trump, who withdrew the United States from formal climate cooperation last year after calling global warming a hoax, ⁠has said investing in Venezuela's oil can bolster national security by increasing Western Hemisphere energy supplies.

Earlier on Thursday (November 12, 2026), British Prime ‌Minister Andy Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war with Ukraine showed the need for countries to switch from fossil fuels to clean energy.

"It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed ‌to prices we cannot control," he said. "The shift to clean energy is the only route ​to energy security."

Thursday (November 12, 2026) is the fifth day of the two-week COP31 conference where representatives from nearly 200 countries ⁠are trying to agree a deal to improve progress in tackling climate ⁠change.

A UN report last month found the world was on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees ‌Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

articles.title: Indonesia's Vice President resigns as eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents submitted by Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements
Indonesia's Vice President resigned on Thursday (November 12, 2026) as questions grew over his eligibility for the office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials.

Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, submitted his resignation to the leadership of the People's Consultative Assembly, the country's highest legislative body, at the Parliament building in the capital, Jakarta.
The academic credentials investigation was apparently not related to investigations into allegations that top police officials had been involved in wiretapping targeting the president.

Under Indonesia's Constitution, a Vice Presidential vacancy does not trigger a new election. The office remains vacant until the People's Consultative Assembly elects a replacement from two candidates nominated by the president within 60 days.

Mr. Raka had offered to resign on Tuesday during a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, saying he wanted to avoid a prolonged political controversy. But a Cabinet minister said the president urged Mr. Raka at the time to defend himself and it wasn't clear if he accepted the resignation offer.
The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents Mr. Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.
A subsequent petition, submitted on Wednesday to the House leadership by 120 lawmakers from eight political parties, began a parliamentary process that could lead to his impeachment.

Under Indonesian law, House leaders must establish a special committee to examine whether Mr. Raka has violated the Constitution by serving as Vice President, despite allegedly failing to meet election requirements. If lawmakers determine there is sufficient basis for the accusation, the House must ask the Constitutional Court to rule on whether a constitutional violation has occurred.

articles.title: Karnataka plans app to track used cooking oil, prevent re-entry into food chain
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Food Safety Department to develop a digital system within three months; pilot project in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru and Hubballi

Karnataka’s Health Department is developing a mobile application to track the collection, sale and reuse of used cooking oil , with the objective of preventing its re-entry into the food chain, Health Minister U.T. Khader said on Thursday (November 12).

The application, which is expected to be developed within three months, will create a digital trail from the point at which cooking oil is purchased by hotels and other food business operators to its eventual disposal or transfer to authorised agencies for industrial use, Mr. Khader said.

The initiative is aimed at addressing the illegal diversion of used cooking oil, which is sometimes collected for industrial purposes such as soap manufacturing and biodiesel production but allegedly finds its way back to small hotels and eateries for reuse in cooking.

Addressing presspersons in Bengaluru, Mr. Khader said the Food Safety and Drugs Administration Department would manage the application. All manufacturers and food business operators would be required to register on the platform. The department would initially conduct a trial run in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru and Hubballi.

Explaining the proposed mechanism, he said hotels and other establishments would have to enter details of the quantity of fresh cooking oil purchased, its source, and the quantity of used oil generated. They would have to record the identity of the person or agency to whom the used oil was handed over.
The collectors, in turn, would have to upload details of whom they sold the oil to, the quantity transferred, and the amount paid.

“If a hotel uses 500 litres of oil in a month, it must account for the 50 to 75 litres of used oil generated, assuming a 10% to 15% recovery. It must submit details of whom it handed over the used oil to. The person who collects it must record whom they sold it to. The entire chain has to be tracked,” he said.
The Minister said the system was necessary because the department currently lacked reliable data on the movement of used cooking oil and its eventual destination.
Under the proposed arrangement, used oil collected from food establishments would have to be channelled towards authorised industrial uses rather than being sold back to food businesses.
Mr. Khader said some agencies authorised to collect used cooking oil for industrial purposes were diverting a portion of it to small hotels.

articles.title: Deceased TGSRTC driver’s son gets job
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: TGSRTC driver K. Shankar Goud succumbed to burn injuries in April during a strike
The son of a Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) worker, K. Shankar Goud, who succumbed to burn injuries in April 2026, was given a letter of appointment on Thursday.

Mr. Goud, who was from Narasampet, was a driver at the local bus depot. He had attempted to immolate himself during the TGSRTC workers’ stir, and was immediately rushed to the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Warangal. But, given his critical condition, he was later shifted to Hyderabad where he succumbed.
The Telangana government assured Mr. Goud’s family of financial assistance and a job. Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar had condoled his death.
On Thursday, Mr. Prabhakar and TGSRTC Chairman Y. Nagi Reddy handed over the letter of appointment to the deceased’s son Hemanth Goud.

Mr. Prabhakar appreciated the effort of the TGSRTC employees to raise funds for Mr. Goud’s family. He said that the Telangana goverment was committed to help TGSRTC workers and that the letter of appointment was a part of its responsibility.
He reiterated that issues of TGSRTC workers, or instances of indiscipline should be escalated to senior officers and physical attacks against staff would not be tolerated.
Touching upon the integrity of TGSRTC workers, he said that they had returned lost items worth several lakhs to their rightful owners.
“The unity shown by the RTC staff in supporting Shankar Goud’s family through financial aid is commendable,” he said.

articles.title: Parents who work for children’s future end up in old age homes, says writer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Children’s Day programme highlights need to preserve cultural values, protect children from excessive academic pressure and phone use

Parents who work hard and make immense sacrifices to ensure that their children settle abroad or secure prestigious positions often end up spending their later years in old age homes, a growing social concern, Kannada novelist and writer Kumbar Veerabhadrappa said.
He was speaking after inaugurating a district-level Children’s Day programme for 2026-27 organised at the Zilla Panchayat Conference Hall in Ballari on Thursday.

Expressing concern over the growing number of old age homes in the country, Mr. Veerabhadrappa said that the present education system is increasingly centred on money, leaving little room for human values and respect for elders.

He stressed the need to preserve village traditions, folk arts and cultural practices and pass them onto future generations. He also described people donating the bodies of their dead elderly parents to medical colleges as a commendable practice that others should consider adopting.

Appreciating the State government’s attention to child welfare, nutrition and the quality of food provided at anganwadis, he said that Karnataka is giving serious thought to these issues from scientific and rational perspectives.
He expressed concern that the semester-based education system and the excessive homework assigned to children are affecting their opportunities to play and develop communication skills.
Mobile phones, he said, have also become a major obstacle to the all-round development of children.
Urging officials to go beyond routine meetings and administrative pressures, Mr. Veerabhadrappa called for serious attention to the health, safety and overall development of the younger generation.

Senior Civil Judge and Member-Secretary of the District Legal Services Authority Rajesh N. Hosamane, who also spoke on the occasion, stressed the importance of inculcating moral values, discipline, traditions and respect for culture among children.
He expressed concern over the increasing tendency among underage children to ride motorcycles and urged parents to prevent minors from driving vehicles.

articles.title: Owaisi, Chandrashekhar Azad announce Samajik Parivartan Morcha for 2027 U.P. Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: We welcome the ‘Social Change Front’. Change must occur at the societal level, but true success will only be achieved when the “Political Change Front” is activated, says Akhilesh Yadav

All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief Chandrashekhar Azad on Thursday announced a new political alliance, the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
This is the first declared non-NDA, non-INDIA political front in U.P., with both parties considered minor players eyeing the consolidation of marginalised voters in the State.

“We have been holding discussions for quite some time. Under the alliance framework, we have declared Chandrashekhar Azad as our chief ministerial candidate. Our aim is to address the issues faced by the people of Uttar Pradesh. The BJP has ruined U.P.’s education system. The future of the State’s youth is being destroyed, and unemployment has become the norm. Other political parties failed to stop the BJP in Uttar Pradesh, as witnessed in the elections of 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022, and 2024. Our alliance will emerge as a strong alternative. We are hopeful and will work hard to achieve our political objectives,” said Mr. Owaisi, the Hyderabad Lok Sabha MP.

“This is not a third front, but a front for social change. Our alliance is strong on the ground, and it will grow even stronger. It is an alliance of deprived, downtrodden, marginalised, oppressed, and exploited people and groups. Our promise is to eradicate poverty and helplessness, and to put an end to the caste-based violence and oppression inflicted upon us in Uttar Pradesh,” said Mr. Azad, Lok Sabha MP from Nagina.

He said that those who spoke of uplifting poor, marginalised social groups and bringing them into the mainstream went on to become MLAs, MPs, Chief Ministers, and even Prime Ministers. “Yet, these marginalised communities remain exactly where they have always been. The truth is that governments kept changing, announcements kept being made, and even today, the Bahujan community remains deprived of basic amenities; in Uttar Pradesh, these communities face injustice due to bulldozer Raj,” he added.

The Nagina MP was also asked if he would join hands with the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress. “Our heart is not small. The main opposition alliance failed to defeat the BJP in previous elections. I urge other parties to join our coalition to defeat the BJP. However, there is a lot of arrogance; still, we remain open to a united front against the BJP,” said Mr. Azad.
Mr. Azad and Mr. Owaisi arrived separately in Lucknow for the joint press conference.
Meanwhile, SP president Akhilesh Yadav welcomed the new political front.

“We welcome the ‘Social Change Front’. Change must occur at the societal level, but true success will only be achieved when the “Political Change Front” is activated. We will support anyone who truly fights against communal forces for the betterment of society and raises the voice of the PDA community, in making their honest voice reach the public. One benefit of this for the opposition is that those who used to vote for communal forces after being swayed by emotional rhetoric and deception will no longer turn to them. These naive people who have been misled and voted will now have another option. This will result in a further loss of 2-3% votes for the BJP. The BJP will be left with nothing. The public understands the truth of those whose sole aim is to generate excitement through words and statements. The truth is that such protests strengthen democracy, provided they are motivated by the welfare of one’s own community, not by the ulterior motives of a third party. If someone becomes a puppet of politics, the public can even have their bail forfeited. Hopefully, the practice of “vote-contracting” in politics will end, and everyone will work for the true benefit of their community,” wrote Mr. Yadav on X.
The Dalit and minority communities account for over 40% of the State’s total electorate.

articles.title: Mysuru set to get one of India’s most advanced LED-dome planetariums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi to inaugurate COSMOS Planetarium on Friday; next generation technology to offer immersive space experience, boost science education and tourism

Mysuru is all set to emerge as a hub for astronomy education and science outreach with the launch of COSMOS Planetarium, one of the country’s first planetariums to feature next-generation LED Dome technology, offering an immersive 8K visual experience.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the planetarium, located at the foothills of Chamundi Hill, on Friday.

Unlike conventional planetariums that use projection-based systems, the LED Dome use a dense array of direct-emission LED panels to deliver seamless ultra high-resolution visuals across the entire curved surface of the dome, providing viewers with an immersive experience of the universe.

An outdoor exhibition area featuring ISRO exhibits and astronomical models inspired by Jantar Mantar, along with an amphitheatre for science discussions and cultural productions, will add to the facilities.

articles.title: Teacher assaulted as student groups clash during arts festival
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred around noon at Parudur Higher Secondary School, when students from the host school and Government Vocational Higher Secondary School, Koppam, clashed on the festival venue

Police resorted to a lathicharge after a clash broke out between students of two schools during the Pattambi sub-district school arts festival at Parudur Higher Secondary School, Nadaparamba, on Thursday. The unrest later spilled into the school building, where a teacher who tried to intervene was assaulted.

The incident occurred around noon at Parudur Higher Secondary School, when students from the host school and Government Vocational Higher Secondary School, Koppam, clashed on the festival venue. As tensions escalated, police from Thrithala resorted to a lathi-charge to disperse the students.

Following this, the students moved into the school building, where the clash continued. Ansil, a temporary physical education teacher at Government Vocational Higher Secondary School, Koppam, was allegedly assaulted while attempting to separate the students and prevent further violence. A group of students reportedly surrounded the teacher and kicked him during the incident.
Teachers and local residents present at the venue intervened and brought the situation under control.

articles.title: It was a busy October for birdwatchers in Tiruchi as some species show up after 50 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A broader regional compilation indicates that Tiruchi district plays host to over 300 bird species; variations in avian migration patterns reflect long-term climate change
Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler | Photo Credit: S. Harish Sundhar
Dark sided Flycatcher. | Photo Credit: S. Harish Sundhar
A wide range of migratory birds visited Tiruchi district in October, with some being spotted here after 50 years, showing the potential of the region’s varied landscape as an avian haven.

Birdwatcher S. Harish Sundhar, a postgraduate in Environmental Science from Tiruchi, recorded uncommon to rare migratory birds such as Eurasian Wryneck, Siberian Stonechat, Paddyfield Warbler, Eastern Yellow Wagtail, and Richard’s Pipit in the past month.

“I recorded sighting a Long-tailed Shrike on October 17. According to available historical records on eBird, the species had previously been documented only twice in Tiruchi, on January 23 and February 6, 1975, both at Umaiyalpuram. The latest sighting represents the third documented occurrence in the district and the first recorded since February 1975, after more than 51 years,” Mr. Sundhar told The Hindu.
October also saw the first documented district records of three species: Bank Swallow on October 11, Dark-sided Flycatcher on October 12, and Pallas’s Grasshopper Warbler on October 17.
A broader regional compilation indicates that Tiruchi district plays host to over 300 bird species, largely due to its geographical diversity.

“Wetland and aquatic habitats around Tiruchi support an array of wintering birds. The Bank Swallow, for instance, was recorded at Kiliyur Lake, on October 11. Other notable species recorded at the lake included Greater Spotted Eagle, Osprey, Eastern Yellow Wagtail, and Western Marsh Harriers. These observations highlight the lake’s importance as a habitat supporting a diverse assemblage of migratory waterbirds and raptors,” said Mr. Sundhar.

Variations in avian migration patterns are an indicator of long-term climate change that need greater study. “Though grasslands and other wooded areas are slowly getting swallowed up by urban development, they are an important habitat for birds and other small animals. Tiruchi district’s birdwatching enthusiasts should make an effort to document and report the various bird species and publish a pictorial guide. This will help us to conserve our natural environment for future generations as well,” said Justus Joshua, senior fellow, Indian Regional Association for Landscape Ecology.

Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler | Photo Credit: S. Harish Sundhar

A wide range of migratory birds visited Tiruchi district in October, with some being spotted here after 50 years, showing the potential of the region’s varied landscape as an avian haven.

Birdwatcher S. Harish Sundhar, a postgraduate in Environmental Science from Tiruchi, recorded uncommon to rare migratory birds such as Eurasian Wryneck, Siberian Stonechat, Paddyfield Warbler, Eastern Yellow Wagtail, and Richard’s Pipit in the past month.

“I recorded sighting a Long-tailed Shrike on October 17. According to available historical records on eBird, the species had previously been documented only twice in Tiruchi, on January 23 and February 6, 1975, both at Umaiyalpuram. The latest sighting represents the third documented occurrence in the district and the first recorded since February 1975, after more than 51 years,” Mr. Sundhar told The Hindu.

October also saw the first documented district records of three species: Bank Swallow on October 11, Dark-sided Flycatcher on October 12, and Pallas’s Grasshopper Warbler on October 17.

A broader regional compilation indicates that Tiruchi district plays host to over 300 bird species, largely due to its geographical diversity.

“Wetland and aquatic habitats around Tiruchi support an array of wintering birds. The Bank Swallow, for instance, was recorded at Kiliyur Lake, on October 11. Other notable species recorded at the lake included Greater Spotted Eagle, Osprey, Eastern Yellow Wagtail, and Western Marsh Harriers. These observations highlight the lake’s importance as a habitat supporting a diverse assemblage of migratory waterbirds and raptors,” said Mr. Sundhar.

Variations in avian migration patterns are an indicator of long-term climate change that need greater study. “Though grasslands and other wooded areas are slowly getting swallowed up by urban development, they are an important habitat for birds and other small animals. Tiruchi district’s birdwatching enthusiasts should make an effort to document and report the various bird species and publish a pictorial guide. This will help us to conserve our natural environment for future generations as well,” said Justus Joshua, senior fellow, Indian Regional Association for Landscape Ecology.

articles.title: Retail inflation crosses RBI’s upper limit for first time in two years, comes in at 6.1% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Consumer Price Index saw almost all categories hit series highs as inflation spread across sectors of the economy

Retail inflation rose to 6.1% in October 2026, crossing the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper threshold for the first time in two years. The continued uptick in inflation, while driven by food and fuel prices, has now spread to nearly all sectors, data released by the government on Thursday shows.

The RBI targets an inflation rate of 4% with a comfort band of 2% higher or lower than figure. Inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) last crossed this upper threshold of 6% in October 2024, when it came in at 6.2%. Retail inflation in October 2026 was the highest since then.

The new series of the CPI, with a base year of 2024, has sectoral data that goes back to only January 2026, which means a historical analysis is possible only up to that point. Within that, the latest data shows inflation across most categories rose to series highs in October 2026.

“Although inflation remains predominantly supply-driven, stronger consumer demand pull associated with festive-season purchases may have added to price pressures, reinforcing the RBI’s decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%,” Pranjal Ghate, economist at Brickwork Ratings said, referring to the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) latest decision in early October 2026.

The data shows that inflation in the food and beverages category rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026, the highest in the series. Coupled with this, rising fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose to 5.8% in October, a series high.

As a result of accelerating food and transport prices, inflation in the restaurant and accommodation services category jumped to 10.1% in October, the first time it has come in at double-digits in the new series.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, some food prices could rise further in the coming months.

“The ongoing harvest prospects will throw more light on how food prices behave,” Mr. Sabnavis said. “Area under cultivation was lower for rice, maize, oilseeds, cotton and sugarcane. It has also been reported that pulses production, especially tur, could be lower this time, which can lead to a spike in prices.”
Apart from food and fuel, the data shows that other aspects of day-to-day life have also seen prices rising at a faster pace.

Clothing and footwear, for example, saw inflation coming in at nearly 5% in October 2026 — the highest in this series — from 3.9% in the previous month. The ‘furnishings, household equipment, and routine household maintenance’ category saw inflation quicken to 3.9% in October, also a series high.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the ₹2,50,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: New shark species identified in Indian Ocean after decades of misclassification
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The researchers identified the species Indian Bramble Shark, named Echinorhinus roinee
A deep-sea shark found in Indian Ocean waters and long believed to be identical to its Atlantic counterpart has been identified as a distinct species by Indian scientists.

Named Echinorhinus roinee, or the Indian Bramble Shark, the species was identified by researchers from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) and the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), a ZSI statement said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
The discovery marks an important step towards understanding the rich but largely unexplored marine biodiversity of the Indian Ocean.
The research findings have been published in the journal ‘Records of the Zoological Survey of India’ (Volume 126, Issue 1S, 2026).
The specimens were collected at Sakthikulangara Fishing Harbour in Kollam, Kerala, where the sharks were brought ashore as accidental catches by deep-sea shrimp trawlers.
These sharks live along the underwater slopes of the continental shelf at depths of 350 to 450 metres and can grow up to three metres in length.
It has a dark brown to almost black body covered with large, thorn-like structures on its skin.

As the shark grows older, these structures join together to form plates with several pointed edges. Scientists found that the newly identified species has larger eyes, bigger pelvic fins and a longer region between its snout and gills compared to related species.
DNA tests also confirmed that it is genetically different from the Atlantic bramble shark (Echinorhinus brucus) and the Pacific prickly shark (Echinorhinus cookei).

Genetic records from other regions suggest that the newly identified species may also be found in waters off Oman, Sri Lanka and Thailand, indicating that its distribution is not limited to the Indian coast, the statement said.

articles.title: Study suggests not all obesity means ill-health
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study follows a proposal last year from experts and medical organisations to move obesity diagnosis beyond just body mass index (BMI), based on a person’s weight and height, to include body fat and broader health

Only between a quarter and a third of people currently diagnosed with obesity should be considered as in poor health, according to a new study that joins calls to overhaul how the condition is diagnosed.

The study, published in Nature on Wednesday, follows a proposal last year from experts and medical organisations to move obesity diagnosis beyond just body mass index (BMI), based on a person’s weight and height, to include body fat and broader health.

The study attempts to show what this new definition could mean for diagnosis levels, prevalence, and ultimately, treatment, for a condition the World Health Organization currently estimates affects more than one billion people globally.

Obesity can be a risk factor for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver and kidney disease and cancer. The study suggests defining it as pre-clinical, when the condition is largely a risk factor, and clinical, when it is causing ill health.

Using data from almost 850,000 adults from China, Britain, the US and Spain, the study estimates that under the new framework, 1% to 3% of those defined as obese using BMI alone would not be, while another 5% to 9%, with higher body fat for example, would be diagnosed with the condition. Across a population, this could affect tens of millions of people.
The study’s senior author Francesco Rubino, professor and chair of metabolic and bariatric surgery at King’s College London, said the inaccuracy of BMI measurements was well-known.

“But we haven’t so far got a better system,” he said. That is what the new framework aims to do, he added, saying it could “provide a meaningful clinical characterisation of obesity that can inform care and policy.”

The new framework proposes measuring body fat, including by waist circumference, as well as BMI, and considering if a patient has any organ dysfunction linked to weight, like heart or liver problems, before making a diagnosis.

This means some people with high BMI alone would not be classed as having obesity. Those who have high body fat and high BMI would be diagnosed with “pre-clinical obesity”, and those who also have organ dysfunction would have “clinical obesity” – considered an active disease that would usually require more urgent treatment.
Under these criteria, only on average roughly 27% of people with obesity across the four studied countries have clinical obesity, the study estimated – representing around 8.5% of all adults.

The study follows a proposal last year from experts and medical organisations to move obesity diagnosis beyond just body mass index (BMI), based on a person’s weight and height, to include body fat and broader health

Only between a quarter and a third of people currently diagnosed with obesity should be considered as in poor health, according to a new study that joins calls to overhaul how the condition is diagnosed.

The study, published in Nature on Wednesday, follows a proposal last year from experts and medical organisations to move obesity diagnosis beyond just body mass index (BMI), based on a person’s weight and height, to include body fat and broader health.

The study attempts to show what this new definition could mean for diagnosis levels, prevalence, and ultimately, treatment, for a condition the World Health Organization currently estimates affects more than one billion people globally.

Obesity can be a risk factor for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver and kidney disease and cancer. The study suggests defining it as pre-clinical, when the condition is largely a risk factor, and clinical, when it is causing ill health.

Using data from almost 850,000 adults from China, Britain, the US and Spain, the study estimates that under the new framework, 1% to 3% of those defined as obese using BMI alone would not be, while another 5% to 9%, with higher body fat for example, would be diagnosed with the condition. Across a population, this could affect tens of millions of people.

The study’s senior author Francesco Rubino, professor and chair of metabolic and bariatric surgery at King’s College London, said the inaccuracy of BMI measurements was well-known.

“But we haven’t so far got a better system,” he said. That is what the new framework aims to do, he added, saying it could “provide a meaningful clinical characterisation of obesity that can inform care and policy.”

The new framework proposes measuring body fat, including by waist circumference, as well as BMI, and considering if a patient has any organ dysfunction linked to weight, like heart or liver problems, before making a diagnosis.

This means some people with high BMI alone would not be classed as having obesity. Those who have high body fat and high BMI would be diagnosed with “pre-clinical obesity”, and those who also have organ dysfunction would have “clinical obesity” – considered an active disease that would usually require more urgent treatment.

Under these criteria, only on average roughly 27% of people with obesity across the four studied countries have clinical obesity, the study estimated – representing around 8.5% of all adults.

articles.title: Phage therapy shows promise against antimicrobial resistance, says expert
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy Koganti, sepsis and infectious diseases specialist at SHRI Hospital, Guntur, says that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail

Phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to selectively eliminate harmful bacteria, holds significant potential in combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR), said Dr. Kalyan Chakravarthy Koganti, sepsis and infectious diseases specialist at SHRI Hospital, Guntur.

He said this while sharing his research experience during a press release, after presenting his team's scientific findings at an international symposium jointly organised by the Chinese University of Hong Kong and reputed biomedical research journals.

Dr. Kalyan said his team's research presentation on phage therapy received appreciation from participants at the symposium. Dr. Sutharsan Govindarajan, associate professor and phage biologist, SRM University-A.P., also presented research conducted by the team.

He described the event as an enriching learning experience, particularly the discussions on the wider applications of bacteriophages in diagnostics and therapy, including cancer research. Chuanbin Mao, chair of the symposium, has been researching bacteriophages for 25 years and has contributed extensively to scientific literature, he said.
Dr. Kalyan noted that bacteriophages selectively target disease-causing bacteria without harming human beings, making them promising alternatives when antibiotics fail.

His team has administered phage therapy to a few patients at its centre with encouraging results. In collaboration with SRM University-A.P. and Szeged University, Hungary, the team has been working to advance its availability in India.

articles.title: New blood test finds early risk for ovarian cancer
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: In women with genetic risk factors for ovarian cancer, approximately 72% of positive results would be accurate, while negative results would be correct nearly 100% of the time

A molecular signal in the blood helps identify microscopic changes that precede the development of ovarian cancer, researchers have found, in a potential diagnostic breakthrough for a disease often discovered after it has already spread.
For decades, efforts to detect ovarian cancer earlier have focused on finding smaller tumours, the researchers noted in their report published on Tuesday in Nature Medicine .

“We asked a fundamentally different question: What if we could identify the earliest molecular warning signs before invasive cancer even develops?” study leader Rajan Gogna of the Hoag Family Cancer Institute in Newport Beach, California, said in a statement. Ovarian cancer often begins with microscopic changes in the lining of the fallopian tubes.

The precancerous lesions are known as serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC). The new study found that women with this precursor condition have elevated blood levels of an RNA molecule called Tu-Stroma.

When researchers measured Tu-Stroma in blood, they detected STIC in 92.3% of affected women and correctly identified 98.2% of healthy women. In women with genetic risk factors for ovarian cancer, approximately 72% of positive results would be accurate, while negative results would be correct nearly 100% of the time, they reported. “For women at high risk, this could transform how we approach prevention,” co-author Esha Madan, also of Hoag, said in a statement.

Many such women face difficult decisions about preventive surgery to remove their fallopian tubes and ovaries. “Today, decisions about preventive surgery are largely guided by inherited risk, without knowing whether precancerous lesions are actually present,” Madan said. “Our discovery could eventually provide that missing biological information.”

fullParagraphs: To prevent malpractices during the preliminary examinations to be conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) on Sunday for recruiting 319 Gazetted Probationers, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has issued strict instructions to Deputy Commissioners of all districts to impart training to examination staff on the lines of election duty.

In a virtual meeting to review the examination preparations with the DCs and Superintendents of Police on Thursday, the Chief Minister also directed them to file a compliance report on the measures taken for ensuring conduct of examinations in a foolproof manner.

“We have undertaken several reforms in the examination process,” he said, instructing Deputy Commissioners to strictly enforce the guidelines issued by the KPSC. Continuous surveillance must be maintained through CCTV cameras at all examination centres, he said.

He instructed the Police Department to put in place robust security arrangements similar to those used during police recruitment exams. No unauthorised person should be permitted on the examination centre premises, and even authorised personnel must undergo security checks, he said.

The Chief Minister also instructed officials to assess the sensitivity of each examination centre and deploy staff accordingly. Additional security equipment may be rented, and extra police personnel should be mobilised from other locations if needed. He strictly warned that candidates must not enter examination centres with mobile phones, adding that senior officials themselves will be held accountable for any lapses.

Stating that for the first time, two invigilators will be deployed in every examination hall, the Chief Minister told the authorities concerned that at least one of them must be from a government college. This dual-invigilator system is intended to conduct secondary checks after candidates enter the hall and to maintain strict vigil throughout the exam. He also directed officials to take firm measures to prevent impersonators from appearing for the exam.
The Chief Minister warned that if examination centres located in private and aided colleges are found to have facilitated malpractice, the recognition of such institutions will be cancelled.

Stressing that there must be zero tolerance for the spread of fake news regarding the exam, Mr. Shivakumar directed the Police Department to actively monitor social media. If any rumour surfaces, it must be immediately flagged to officials so that an official clarification can be issued.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal, Naidu, Pawan Kalyan tour Andhra Pradesh Pavilion at CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The leaders try their hand at tribal art and taste Araku Coffee before the summit’s inaugural session

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal, along with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, visited the Andhra Pradesh Pavilion on Thursday (November 12, 2026) before the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam.

Accompanied by State IT and Electronics Minister Nara Lokesh and BJP State chief P.V.N. Madhav, the leaders inspected various stalls showcasing the State’s industrial roadmap, cultural heritage and indigenous products.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Minister Pawan Kalyan, State Minister Nara Lokesh, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal, during their visit to the Andhra Pradesh Pavilion and MSME Exhibition at the 31st CII Partnership Summit, in Visakhapatnam on Thursday. (@JaiTDP X/ANI Photo) | Photo Credit: ANI

During the walkthrough, senior officials briefed the Union Minister and the Chief Minister on the ongoing infrastructure and industrial projects across the Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and Amaravati economic regions.

A big day for Vizag! The world is here as we launch the 31st CII Partnership Summit @CII_PS @FollowCII. And I'm wearing our weavers' pride today, a handloom jacket. Proud to support the hands that keep Andhra's craft traditions alive. Any guesses which craft this represents? #CIIPartnershipSummit2026 #ChooseSpeedChooseAP

Officials also made detailed presentations on the ongoing development works in the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) limits, alongside a digital presentation highlighting the growth trajectory of Visakhapatnam.
The leaders also reviewed an exhibition detailing the expansion of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across different parts of the State.
They visited stalls showcasing the State’s traditional arts and handicrafts, including ‘Tholu Bommalata’ (leather puppetry), Pen Kalamkari and various tribal artworks.
Foreign delegates arrive at the Andhra University Engineering College Grounds in Visakhapatnam for the two-day CII Partnership Summit on Thursday. | Photo Credit: K.R. Deepak
Mr. Naidu briefed Mr. Goyal on a dedicated display honouring eminent personalities from Andhra Pradesh across diverse artistic fields, explaining their respective contributions and mastery.

articles.title: IIT-Madras Pravartak to start free online training programmes for teachers, educators, and school students
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: IIT-Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation, the innovation hub of IIT-Madras, is launching free online training programmes for teachers, educators, and school students.

For teachers and educators, the topics to be covered include career counselling certification training, leadership development programme for educators, and classroom management and student engagement.

School students of Classes 7 to 12 will be given training in emerging technologies such as AI fundamentals, EV and future mobility, fundamentals of entrepreneurship, and design thinking and innovation.

The programmes, launched in association with BodhBridge Education, combines live sessions, case studies, and hands-on activities to enhance problem-solving, creativity, communication, and innovation skills for students.
Registrations for November 2026 and January 2027 cycles have been opened and enrolment can be done at https://bodhbridge.iitmpravartak.org.in.

articles.title: A2B secures $180 million investment from James Murdoch, Uday Shankar-backed Bodhi Tree
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 50-year-old brand has shed a majority stake for this deal

Homegrown food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan, popularly known as A2B, has secured investments to the tune $180 million (over ₹1,600 crore) from Bodhi Tree Systems, a firm co-founded by James Murdoch, the younger son of media baron Rupert Murdoch, and Uday Shankar.

The 50-year-old brand has shed a majority stake for this deal. An industry source said that the deal values A2B at roughly $350 million. And from now, Uday Shankar will serve as Chairperson of A2B’s new Board of Directors. Veda Corporate Advisors acted as the exclusive financial advisor to A2B.

Vishnu Shankar, from the A2B promoter family, confirmed the news and told The Hindu that the funds would be utilised for expanding into newer markets both nationally and internationally. Currently, the food chain serves south Indian vegetarian dishes and ​sweets. Mr. Shankar said that the western region of India and the European market are among the key markets the company is looking to tap. “We also want to expand our retail presence. And for this, we will be modernising our factories in Chennai and Bengaluru. We are also exploring the possibility of setting up another factory to cater to the retail and export markets,” Mr. Shankar said.

Founded in the late 1970s by K.T. Venkatesan and K.T. Srinivasa Raja from Rajapalayam, A2B has a strong foothold in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and a growing presence across India. It runs about 160 restaurants and sweet-and-savoury stores in India, with 32 overseas outlets in markets like Singapore, the United States and Australia. It also sells packaged sweets and snacks through retail and online channels. The company is headquartered in Chennai and employs more than 15,000 people. A2B is Bodhi Tree’s third investment, after ALLEN Career Institute and JioStar.

Balachandar R., Director of Junior Kuppanna, said: “There is treasure trove of value creation in PE equity & capital markets for regional legacy brands. Haldiram and A2B has only scratched the surface. I foresee at least 100 listed brands in F&B and food space in the next decade.” It maybe recalled that Mr. Balachandar was the advisor to the Dindigul Thalappakatti deal which happened in 2019. The hotel chain which is famous for its biryani had raised ₹260 crore from CX Partners, a private equity firm.

articles.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26 new roads as part of ICBR-III

Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu .

Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said. The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details.
This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China.

The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China.

The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh.

Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh.

articles.title: U.S. envoys meet Putin at Kremlin following Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The talks produced no visible breakthrough in ending the nearly five years of large-scale hostilities, which began on February 24, 2022, after the fighting initially started in 2014 in eastern Ukraine

U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys arrived at the Kremlin on Thursday (November 12, 2026) for talks with President Vladimir Putin, as Washington sought to generate new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between the Russian and Ukrainian delegations.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Mr.Trump's son-in-law, brokered the talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which were the first direct discussions between Russian and Ukrainian officials in nine months as the push for peace stalled this year.
The talks wrapped up on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) with an agreement on a large exchange of prisoners, with the exact number still to be agreed.

The talks produced no visible breakthrough in ending the nearly five years of large-scale hostilities, which began on February 24, 2022, after the fighting initially started in 2014 in eastern Ukraine.
But Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff appeared keen to seize the moment and went straight to the Kremlin.

Mr. Kushner said that one of the goals of the meeting with Mr. Putin is to get the Russian leader's blessing for European representatives to be part of the talks, which are looking at the continent's broader security arrangements.
The U.S. and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are looking for Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.

At the moment, Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations. Moscow complains that Europe is financing and supplying weaponry to Ukraine and is part of the problem holding up a deal.

Many in Europe see the inclusion of Russia in discussions about European security as an unwelcome concession to Mr. Putin, who has described NATO's eastward expansion as a top security threat to his country. Moscow has demanded that the trans-Atlantic alliance's troops be pulled back from Russia's borders.
Some analysts say negotiators may be looking to grant Russia concessions on NATO's strategy in return for peace in Ukraine — a possibility that has alarmed European governments.
